definition_zh: 目录；目录册；一系列；编入目录
definition_en: a book or list that names things in order, especially goods or library holdings, or to enter items into such a list
core_image: 一页页排好的条目，像账簿一样整齐
scene: 拍卖行整理本季的拍品。 The auction house printed a thick catalogue of paintings.
sceneCN: 这里 catalogue 指「目录册」（第 1 个义项：装订成册的条目清单）；句意是拍卖行印了一本厚厚的画作目录。

senses.title: A book listing items
senses.definition: a printed book or document that lists goods, works of art or books in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序列出商品、艺术品或书籍的印刷册子或文件
senses.example: The gallery sent me its new catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊给我寄来了新目录。
senses.why: The Greek list word was first spoken, then written, and finally bound as a book.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语的清单词先从口头念出，再写下来，最后装订成册。

senses.title: A long series of events
senses.definition: a continuous series of things, especially unpleasant ones, that seem to be counted off
senses.definitionCN: 连续发生的一串事情，尤指像是被逐项数出的不快之事
senses.example: The year was a catalogue of mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年是一连串错误的集合。
senses.why: If a catalogue counts items, then a year full of faults can itself be read as a catalogue.
senses.whyCN: 既然目录是逐项清点，那么满是过失的一年本身也能读成一份目录。

senses.title: To enter items in a list
senses.definition: to record objects or works in an ordered list, often with numbers and descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 把物品或作品记入有序清单，常附编号与说明
senses.example: They catalogued the letters before storing them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们先把信件编目，然后才归档。
senses.why: To catalogue is to do the counting work that produces a catalogue.
senses.whyCN: 编目就是做那份清点工作，从而产生一份目录。

intro.en: Catalogue keeps the French spelling of the Greek list word, and its -ue ending still marks the British form today.
intro.cn: catalogue 保留了希腊语清单词的法语拼写，结尾的 -ue 至今是英式拼写的标志。

items.en: Katalogos meant a list or register, from kata and legein, to say or count.
items.cn: 希腊语 katalogos 意为清单或名录，由 kata 与 legein（说、点数）构成。

items.en: Catalogus carried the word into the written culture of the Roman world.
items.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 把该词带入罗马世界的书写文化。

items.en: Catalogue gave English the -ue spelling that British usage still prefers.
items.cn: 法语 catalogue 给英语留下了英式用法偏爱的 -ue 拼写。

items.en: Catalogue is recorded as a list of names or books arranged for reference.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语中，catalogue 已有按序排列名称或书籍的记录。

items.en: Art dealers and libraries make the printed catalogue a standard tool.
items.cn: 十九世纪艺术品商人与图书馆把印刷目录变成标准工具。

items.en: The phrase a catalogue of disasters fixes the figurative series sense.
items.cn: 短语 a catalogue of disasters 固定了比喻性的「一连串」义。

note.en: The look-alike group stays with the -ue spelling and its derivatives, and the meaning group gives other records.
note.cn: 形近组留在 -ue 拼写及其派生词内，近义组给出其他记录形式。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same word
a person who compiles a catalogue
the process of listing items
an official list kept as a record
a detailed list of goods in stock
a book listing names, addresses or services
entries.definitionCN: 列出名称、地址或服务的册子

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the French -ue ending, the auction phrases and the disaster idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用法语式 -ue 词尾、拍卖场搭配以及灾难习语。

normal.en: The -ue ending is the British mark, just as in colour and theatre.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ue 是英式标志，就像 colour 与 theatre 的拼写。

normal.en: Catalogue and dialogue share the Greek root legein, to speak or count.
normal.cn: catalogue 与 dialogue 共享希腊语词根 legein（说或点数）。

normal.en: Auction catalogue and exhibition catalogue fix the printed-book sense.
normal.cn: auction catalogue 与 exhibition catalogue 固定了印刷册子义。

normal.en: A catalogue of disasters is a whole year of trouble read aloud.
normal.cn: a catalogue of disasters 就是把一整年的麻烦逐条念出来。

normal.en: Catalogue numbers give each listed work a small address of its own.
normal.cn: 目录编号给每件列出的作品一个小地址。

abstract.en: Picture a thick book with gilt numbers down the spine.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书，书脊上印着烫金编号。

abstract.en: Picture an auctioneer tapping a page of listed paintings.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖师敲着写满画作的那一页。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of boxes, each labelled with a neat number.
abstract.cn: 想象一整排箱子，每只都标着整齐的编号。

examples.en: The catalogue lists every piece in the show.
examples.cn: 目录列出了展览中的每件作品。

examples.en: She found the price in the auction catalogue.
examples.cn: 她在拍卖目录里找到了价格。

examples.en: The collection was catalogued over ten years.
examples.cn: 这批藏品用了十年时间编目。

dict_mnemonic.text: catalogue 里的 log 是记录：把展品一件件记进本子，就成了一本目录册。

root: 与 catalog 同源，出自希腊语 katalogos（清单），经拉丁语 catalogus 与法语 catalogue 进入英语，-ue 为法式拼写残留。

sensesIntro.en: A spoken counting-off becomes a printed book, then a year of misfortunes, while the verb names the counting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 口头的逐项点数变成印刷册子，再变成一年的不幸，而动词则指点数这个动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered entries standing in neat rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：编了号、排成整齐行列的条目。

branches.en: The written list is bound and sold as a catalogue.
branches.cn: 写下的清单被装订起来，作为目录册出售。

branches.en: A run of bad events is counted off like entries.
branches.cn: 一连串坏事像条目一样被逐项数出。

branches.en: The verb performs the counting that fills the book.
branches.cn: 动词义执行填入册子的清点工作。

branches.en: Book and action are two sides of the same ordered record.
branches.cn: 册子与动作是同一份有序记录的两面。

branches.en: Both senses rely on the feeling of a long, orderly series.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖「长而有序的一串」这种感觉。

intro.en: Catalogue forms -er and -ing nouns and keeps the French -ue in every British spelling.
intro.cn: catalogue 构成 -er 与 -ing 名词，英式拼写始终保留法语式 -ue。

latinIntro.en: Latin catalogus kept the Greek list word, which French later reshaped as catalogue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 保留了希腊语清单词，法语后来把它改写成 catalogue。

items.example: The cataloguer noted a missing page.
items.exampleCN: 编目员注意到缺了一页。

items.meaning: the same word in American English

items.exampleCN: catalogus 见于中世纪图书馆。

latinEntries.example: Catalogus is the Latin bridge to English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: catalogus 是通向英语的拉丁语桥梁。

definition_zh: 耸肩；表示怀疑；不理会；耸肩动作
definition_en: to raise the shoulders to show doubt or indifference, to dismiss something, or such a movement
core_image: 一个人双肩一抬，嘴角一撇，表示自己也不知道
scene: 他耸耸肩说不知道。 He shrugged and said he did not know.
sceneCN: 这里 shrug 是「耸肩」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他耸耸肩说不知道。

senses.title: To raise the shoulders
senses.definition: to raise the shoulders slightly
senses.definitionCN: 轻轻抬起双肩
senses.example: He shrugged and said he did not know.
senses.exampleCN: 他耸耸肩说不知道。
senses.why: This is the basic gesture.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的手势义项。

senses.title: To show doubt
senses.definition: to use the gesture to show doubt
senses.definitionCN: 用这个动作表示怀疑
senses.example: She shrugged at my question.
senses.exampleCN: 她对我的问题耸了耸肩。
senses.why: The movement answers a question without words.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作不用语言就回答了问题。

senses.title: To dismiss
senses.definition: to treat something as unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当作不重要
senses.example: He shrugged off the criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他对批评不予理会。
senses.why: The gesture can push a problem away.
senses.whyCN: 这个手势可以把问题推开。

senses.title: The movement
senses.definition: the act of raising the shoulders
senses.definitionCN: 抬起肩膀的动作
senses.example: She answered with a shrug.
senses.exampleCN: 她耸了耸肩作为回答。
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun for the gesture.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为表示该手势的名词。

intro.en: Shrug is a Middle English word whose deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: shrug 是中东英语词，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Shruggen meant to raise the shoulders.
items.cn: shruggen 意为抬起肩膀。

items.en: The word may echo the movement itself.
items.cn: 这个词可能模仿动作本身。

items.en: The gesture became a sign of doubt.
items.cn: 这个手势成为怀疑的标志。

items.en: Shrug off came to mean to dismiss.
items.cn: shrug off 逐渐表示不理会。

items.en: The noun named the movement itself.
items.cn: 名词指动作本身。

note.en: Shrug is compared with similar-looking words and with words for gestures and dismissal.
note.cn: 把 shrug 与形近词以及表示手势和不予理会的词作比较。

entries.definition: to become smaller
to close
a small bush
a movement that means something
to move the head up and down
to decide something is not important

normalIntro.en: A shrug is a sentence spoken with the shoulders.
normalIntro.cn: 耸肩是用肩膀说出的一句话。

normal.en: He shrugged and said he did not know.
normal.cn: 他耸耸肩说不知道。

normal.en: She shrugged at my question.
normal.cn: 她对我的问题耸了耸肩。

normal.en: He shrugged off the criticism.
normal.cn: 他对批评不予理会。

normal.en: She answered with a shrug.
normal.cn: 她耸了耸肩作为回答。

normal.en: Do not shrug away your chance.
normal.cn: 别把机会甩开。

abstract.en: A shrug says what words are too tired to say.
abstract.cn: 耸肩说出了词语累得说不出口的话。

abstract.en: To shrug off a burden is to set it down.
abstract.cn: 甩开负担就是把它放下。

abstract.en: The smallest gesture can close a long argument.
abstract.cn: 最小的手势也能结束一场长争论。

examples.en: He shrugged and said he did not know.
examples.cn: 他耸耸肩说不知道。

examples.en: She answered with a shrug.
examples.cn: 她耸了耸肩作为回答。

examples.en: He shrugged off the criticism.
examples.cn: 他对批评不予理会。

dict_mnemonic.text: shrug 把两个肩膀往上一抬：抬起来表示不知道，抬完放下表示不在乎。

root: 源自中古英语 shruggen（抬肩），核心义「用肩部动作表达态度」。

sensesIntro.en: Shrug means to raise the shoulders, show doubt, dismiss something, or such a movement.
sensesIntro.cn: shrug 意为耸肩、表示怀疑、不理会或耸肩动作。

core.en: Shoulders rise to say what words will not.
core.cn: 双肩抬起，说出词语不愿说的话。

branches.en: The shoulders move upward.
branches.cn: 双肩向上移动。

branches.en: The body admits it does not know.
branches.cn: 身体承认自己不知道。

branches.en: The gesture pushes a problem away.
branches.cn: 这个手势把问题推开。

branches.en: The movement becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 动作变成了名词。

branches.en: Doubt and dismissal share the same small motion.
branches.cn: 怀疑与不理会共享同一个小动作。

intro.en: Shrug builds a small family of gesture words.
intro.cn: shrug 构成表示手势的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shrug is Germanic; Latin gestus, a gesture, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shrug 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 gestus（手势）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She shrugs when she is unsure.
She stood shrugging at the door.

items.meaning: to push away with a shrug

definition_zh: 抱怨；投诉；诉说
definition_en: to say that you are unhappy or not satisfied about something
core_image: 饭桌上有人皱着眉头把盘子往前一推
scene: 楼上整夜装修，邻居第二天一早就去了物业。 She complained about the noise for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 complain 指「投诉；抱怨」（第 1 个义项：表达不满）；句意是她为这噪音抱怨了一周。

senses.title: To say you are unhappy
senses.definition: to say that something is wrong or annoying
senses.definitionCN: 说出某事不对或令人烦
senses.example: He complained about the cold soup.
senses.exampleCN: 他抱怨汤是凉的。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply giving voice to a private displeasure.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项只是把心里的不快说出来。

senses.title: To make a formal protest
senses.definition: to tell an authority that something is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 向管理方说明某事有问题
senses.example: Guests complained to the manager about the room.
senses.exampleCN: 客人向经理投诉房间问题。
senses.why: When the listener has power to act, a complaint becomes a formal claim.
senses.whyCN: 当听者有权处理，抱怨就成了正式投诉。

senses.title: To describe a pain or illness
senses.definition: to say that you feel pain somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 说自己某处疼痛
senses.example: She complained of a headache all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她一上午都在说头痛。
senses.why: Pain, once spoken, becomes a symptom a doctor can read.
senses.whyCN: 疼痛一旦说出，就成了医生能读的症状。

intro.en: Complain comes from Latin plangere, to beat the breast in grief, through Old French complaindre.
intro.cn: complain 经古法语 complaindre 上溯到拉丁语 plangere，意为悲伤地捶胸。

items.en: Plangere meant to strike the breast and lament.
items.cn: plangere 意为捶胸哀叹。

items.en: The word shifted from mourning to voicing any grief.
items.cn: 这个词从哀悼转向说出任何悲伤。

items.en: Old French complaindre brought it into daily speech.
items.cn: 古法语 complaindre 把它带进日常语言。

items.en: English complain first meant to lament a loss.
items.cn: 英语 complain 最初指为损失而哀叹。

items.en: It settled into grumbling, formal protest and naming a pain.
items.cn: 后来它稳定为抱怨、正式投诉与说出病痛。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to complain, and the meaning group ranks grumbling, protesting and formal objection.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 complain 形状相近的词，近义组排出嘟囔、抗议与正式反对。

entries.definition: a statement of dissatisfaction
to finish something
a business firm
to complain in a quiet, bad-tempered way
to say strongly that something is wrong
to express disagreement

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a plate pushed away, then move to a formal complaint and to pain that is finally spoken.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被推开的盘子开始，再走到正式投诉以及终于说出口的疼痛。

normal.en: Complain about a thing, complain to a person, complain of a pain.
normal.cn: 对事情用 complain about，对人用 complain to，说疼痛用 complain of。

normal.en: The noun is complaint, and it is one letter away from complain.
normal.cn: 名词是 complaint，与 complain 只差一点。

normal.en: A complainer finds a flaw in every meal.
normal.cn: 爱抱怨的人每顿饭都能挑出毛病。

normal.en: Complaining to a manager turns a grumble into a case.
normal.cn: 向经理抱怨，就把嘟囔变成了一桩案子。

normal.en: The old root means to beat the breast, so the word began in grief.
normal.cn: 古老词根意为捶胸，所以这个词起于悲伤。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon set down a little too hard.
abstract.cn: 想象勺子被放得稍重了一点。

abstract.en: Picture a guest writing a long note at the front desk.
abstract.cn: 想象客人在前台写一张长长的意见。

abstract.en: Picture a patient pointing at the chest and frowning.
abstract.cn: 想象病人指着胸口皱眉。

examples.en: Customers complained about the slow service.
examples.cn: 顾客抱怨服务太慢。

examples.en: Stop complaining and help me carry this.
examples.cn: 别抱怨了，帮我抬一下这个。

examples.en: He complained of chest pain at midnight.
examples.cn: 他半夜说胸口疼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 complain 记成 com（一起）加 plain（捶胸）：一起捶着胸说委屈，就是抱怨。

root: 源自拉丁语 plangere（捶胸哀叹）与古法语 complaindre，本义是为不幸而捶胸出声，后引申为抱怨、投诉与诉说病痛。

sensesIntro.en: From voicing a small annoyance, to a formal claim, and finally to naming a pain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从说出小小的不快，到正式投诉，最后到说出病痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone at a table pushing the plate away with a frown.
core.cn: 核心意象：饭桌上有人皱着眉头把盘子往前一推。

branches.en: Saying you are unhappy is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 说出自己不开心，是最朴素的义项。

branches.en: A complaint to someone in power becomes official.
branches.cn: 向有权处理的人抱怨，就变成正式的。

branches.en: Pain spoken aloud becomes a symptom.
branches.cn: 疼痛说出口，就成了症状。

branches.en: Both senses begin with the same displeasure.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从同一种不快开始。

branches.en: Both hand the trouble to someone who can act.
branches.cn: 两者都把麻烦交给能处理的人。

intro.en: Complain is a verb from Old French complaindre, built on the Latin lament base plangere.
intro.cn: complain 是来自古法语 complaindre 的动词，建立在拉丁语表示哀叹的词基 plangere 上。

latinIntro.en: The same root survives in plangent, a sound that is loud and mournful.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个词根还留在 plangent 里，指响亮而哀伤的声音。

items.meaning: says he or she is unhappy

items.example: They complained to the front desk.
Complaining will not fix the lift.
The manager knew every complainer by name.
items.exampleCN: 经理叫得出每个爱抱怨的客人的名字。
她的投诉很快得到处理。

items.meaning: a person who makes a formal complaint
items.example: The complainant asked for a refund.

definition_zh: 理想上；最好；理想情况下；以最理想的方式
definition_en: used to describe the best possible situation or outcome, or the standard one would wish to reach
core_image: 一张草图上先画出最完美的布局，再用铅笔在旁边标注现实能建的部分
scene: 设计师先在纸上画出最完美的布局，然后才考虑现实中的限制。 Ideally, the new library would sit at the centre of the campus.
sceneCN: 这里指设想最理想的状态（第 1 个义项：最佳状态）；句意为最理想的情况是，新图书馆坐落在校园的中心。场景要点：纸上的完美布局、后来才考虑的限制、校园中心的位置。

pos.zh: 理想上；最好；理想情况下

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「形象、所见」经拉丁与法语借入，义为「想法、观念」
由观念名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「理想的」
由理想形容词加表示学说体系的名词尾构成，义为「理想主义」
由理想形容词加表示人的名词尾构成，义为「理想主义者」
由理想形容词加动词词尾构成，义为「把……理想化」

senses.title: The best possible state
senses.definition: describes conditions as they would be if nothing stood in the way
senses.definitionCN: 描述在没有阻碍时会呈现的那种状况
senses.example: Ideally, the new library would sit at the centre of the campus.
senses.exampleCN: 最理想的情况是，新图书馆坐落在校园的中心。
senses.why: Idea is an image in the mind, and the ideal is that image at its best.
senses.whyCN: 「观念」是心里的一幅形象，而「理想的」就是那幅形象最好的样子。

senses.title: The goal one aims at
senses.definition: names the standard that a plan or effort is trying to reach, even if it falls short
senses.definitionCN: 指出一项计划或努力试图达到的标准，即使最终达不到
senses.example: Ideally, every student would read the whole corpus before graduating.
senses.exampleCN: 理想的目标是每位学生在毕业前读完整个语料库。
senses.why: A goal is an ideal seen from the side of effort rather than from the side of fact.
senses.whyCN: 目标是从努力那一侧、而不是从事实那一侧看到的理想。

senses.title: Perfectly suited or placed
senses.definition: modifies an adjective or participle to mean perfectly suited to a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 修饰形容词或分词，表示完全适合某个用途
senses.example: The site is ideally placed for a station.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地作为车站的位置再理想不过。
senses.why: This is the manner sense: in an ideal way, not merely as a wish.
senses.whyCN: 这是方式义：以一种理想的方式，而不只是作为愿望。

senses.title: Sentence-initial planning frame
senses.definition: placed first in a plan or proposal to set out the wished-for arrangement before the constraints
senses.definitionCN: 在计划或提案中置于句首，先摆出所期望的安排，再谈限制
senses.example: Ideally, the work would be finished before the rainy season.
senses.exampleCN: 最理想的是，这项工程能在雨季之前完工。
senses.why: A plan states its ideal first so that later compromises can be measured against it.
senses.whyCN: 计划先把理想说出来，日后的让步才好拿它来量。

senses.title: The softened expectation with would
senses.titleCN: 与虚拟式连用的委婉期望
senses.definition: with would or could, softens a request or expectation so that it sounds like a wish rather than a demand
senses.definitionCN: 与虚拟式连用，把请求或期望放软，听起来像愿望而不是要求
senses.example: We would ideally like an answer by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 最理想的是，我们希望在周五之前得到答复。
senses.why: The conditional leaves the other side room to refuse without a quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 条件式给对方留了拒绝的余地，不必吵起来。

senses.title: The opening position in a negotiation
senses.definition: in bargaining, marks the figure or terms one asks for first, knowing that the final result will be lower
senses.definitionCN: 在议价中标记最先提出的数字或条件，明知最终结果会更低
senses.example: Ideally, we would pay nothing for the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 理想的开价是，第一年我们一分钱也不付。
senses.why: An opening figure is an ideal, not a forecast, and both sides know it.
senses.whyCN: 开价是理想，不是预报，这一点双方都明白。

senses.title: The elliptical ideally, yes
senses.definition: in short replies, agrees that something is the best outcome while implying that it may not happen
senses.definitionCN: 在简短回答里承认某事是最好的结果，同时暗示它未必会发生
senses.example: Could both sides sign this week? Ideally, yes.
senses.exampleCN: 双方这周能签字吗？理想上可以。
senses.why: The short answer grants the wish without pretending that the wish is a fact.
senses.whyCN: 简短回答认可了这个愿望，却不假装愿望已成事实。

senses.title: Not the same as preferably
senses.definition: the boundary sense: ideally names the best possible state, while preferably ranks one option above another
senses.definitionCN: 分界义：这个词指出可能达到的最佳状态，而「优先」那个词只是把某个选项排在另一个之上
senses.example: Ideally the room is quiet; preferably it also has daylight.
senses.exampleCN: 最理想的是房间安静；其次最好还有自然光。
senses.why: The best state is not the same as a preference among choices.
senses.whyCN: 最佳状态与在若干选项里挑一个，并不是一回事。

senses.title: Not the same as in theory
senses.definition: the boundary sense: ideally describes a state worth reaching in practice, while in theory describes what principle says, whether or not it can be reached
senses.definitionCN: 分界义：这个词描述一个在实践中值得达到的状态，而「理论上」描述原理怎么说，无论能否达到
senses.example: In theory the system works; ideally it would also be cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 理论上这套系统行得通；最理想的是它还便宜。
senses.why: One is a goal, the other is a principle, and the difference is where each one lives.
senses.whyCN: 一个是目标，一个是原理，差别在于它们各自住在哪里。

intro.en: Ideally is ideal plus -ly. Ideal comes through French idéal from Latin idealis, from Greek idea, a form or appearance, from idein, to see. The adverb marks the way things would be at their best.
intro.cn: ideally 是 ideal 加 -ly。ideal 经法语 idéal 来自拉丁语 idealis，再上溯希腊语 idea「形相、外观」，动词为 idein「看见」。这个副词标记事物处于最好状态时的样子。

items.en: The verb meant to see, and it stands behind idea and the whole family of ideal words.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「看见」，idea 与整个「理想」词族都由它而来。

items.en: The noun named a form or appearance, and later an image in the mind.
items.cn: 这个名词指形相或外观，后来指心里的形象。

items.en: Latin borrowed the noun and used it for a mental pattern or conception.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个名词，用它指心中的模式或概念。

items.en: French formed the adjective for what exists only as a pattern to be reached.
items.cn: 法语构成这个形容词，指只作为待达到的模式而存在的东西。

items.en: English took the adjective and later the noun; the first dates are only approximate.
items.cn: 英语接收了这个形容词，后来又接收其名词用法；首次年代仅为约数。

items.en: The adverb was formed with -ly to set out the best case; the exact date of its first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词由 -ly 构成，用来摆出最好的情形；其首次使用的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the seeing-and-image stem; the second holds the preference and principle words it is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组共享「看见与形象」的词干；第二组是拿来与它比较的偏好与原理说法。

entries.definition: A thought, plan or conception in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 指心里的想法、计划或概念。

entries.definition: The best possible model of something, or existing only as such a model.
entries.definitionCN: 指某事最好的典范，或只作为这种典范而存在的。

entries.definition: The belief that ideals can guide reality, or a philosophical position about mind.
entries.definitionCN: 指相信理想能引导现实的立场，或关于心灵的哲学主张。

entries.definition: A person who holds to ideals, sometimes with the implication of impracticality.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚持理想的人，有时暗含不切实际之意。

entries.definition: From Old English idle, empty or unused; it means without purpose, and has nothing to do with idea.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语中意为「空的、未用的」的词，意为无所事事地，与「观念」毫无关系。

entries.definition: Marks which option is preferred among several, not the best possible state.
entries.definitionCN: 标记若干选项中被偏爱的一个，而不是可能的最佳状态。

entries.definition: According to principle, whether or not it can be achieved in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指依原理而言，无论实践中能否做到。

entries.definition: Sets out a perfect situation while openly admitting that it is not this world.
entries.definitionCN: 摆出一种完美情形，同时公开承认那不是现实世界。

entries.definition: A practical request that asks for something within existing limits.
entries.definitionCN: 一种务实的请求，要求在现有条件下尽量做到。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek verb of seeing, the idea family, and the draftsman's first drawing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用希腊语「看见」的动词、观念词族，以及绘图者画下的第一稿。

normal.en: Idein is to see, idea is what is seen, and ideally is how things look at their best.
normal.cn: 「看见」是看，「观念」是被看见的东西，「理想地」就是事物最好时的样子。

normal.en: Idea, ideal, idealism, idealist and ideally are one family, one root, five jobs.
normal.cn: 观念、理想的、理想主义、理想主义者与理想地：一个词族，一个词根，五份差事。

normal.en: The draftsman's first drawing is the word's home: perfect lines before the site survey.
normal.cn: 绘图者的第一稿是这个词的家乡：先有完美的线，才有场地的勘测。

normal.en: Put it before would and a demand turns into a wish.
normal.cn: 把它放在虚拟式前面，要求就变成愿望。

normal.en: Ideally, yes is an agreement with a door left open.
normal.cn: 「理想上可以」是一句留了门的同意。

abstract.en: An ideal is a map drawn before anyone has walked the ground.
abstract.cn: 理想是一张在无人走过之前就画好的地图。

abstract.en: The word describes the best case and quietly admits it is not the case.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述最好的情形，又悄悄承认它不是眼前的情形。

abstract.en: To name the best is not to promise it, and the word knows the difference.
abstract.cn: 说出最好，并不等于承诺最好；这个词懂这个区别。

examples.en: Ideally, the two departments would share a single archive.
examples.cn: 最理想的是，两个部门共用一个档案库。

examples.en: The hall is ideally suited for small concerts.
examples.cn: 这个厅非常适合举办小型音乐会。

examples.en: Ideally, we would finish the survey before the end of the month.
examples.cn: 最理想的是，我们能在月底之前完成勘测。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「爱迪阿里」——先在纸上画一个最完美的版本，再谈现实：理想上、最好

root: 希腊语 idein「看见」→ idea「形相、观念」→ 拉丁语 idea → 法语 idéal → 英语 ideal，再加副词词尾构成。直接来源清楚；副词首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses differ by what the ideal is doing: describing the best state, naming a goal, modifying a fit, opening a plan, softening a request, setting an opening price, granting in a short reply, and the two boundaries against preferably and in theory.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项按「理想在做什么」分开：描述最佳状态、指出目标、修饰契合程度、开启计划、软化请求、设定开价、简短认可，以及与「优先」「理论上」的两处分界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a perfect layout drawn first on tracing paper, with the buildable part pencilled in beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：先在描图纸上画出完美的布局，再在旁边用铅笔标出现实可建的部分。

branches.en: THE BEST STATE AND THE PERFECT FIT: conditions without obstacles, and a placement that suits a purpose exactly.
branches.cn: 最佳状态与完美契合：没有阻碍的条件，以及恰好适合用途的位置。

branches.en: THE GOAL AND THE PLAN'S OPENING: a standard to reach, set out before the constraints.
branches.cn: 目标与计划的开头：一个待达到的标准，在限制之前先说出来。

branches.en: THE SOFTENED REQUEST AND THE OPENING PRICE: a wish with a conditional, a figure named first.
branches.cn: 软化的请求与开价：带条件式的愿望，以及最先报出的数字。

branches.en: THE SHORT GRANT: yes, with the door left open.
branches.cn: 简短认可：说是，同时把门留着。

branches.en: THE TWO BOUNDARIES: the best state is not a preference, and a goal is not a principle.
branches.cn: 两处分界：最佳状态不是偏好，目标也不是原理。

intro.en: Ideally is a Greek noun of seeing, filtered through Latin and French, wearing an English adjective ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个经拉丁语与法语过滤的希腊「看见」名词，套着英语的形容词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies idein, idea and eidos; Latin borrowed idea and formed idealis, and French turned that into idéal before English took it.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了 idein、idea 与 eidos；拉丁语借入 idea 并构成 idealis，法语把它变成 idéal，英语随后接收。

items.example: The verb is the eye behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族背后的那只眼睛。

items.example: The noun shifts from what is seen to what is conceived.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从「被看见的」转向「被想到的」。

items.example: A related noun names the visible shape itself.
items.exampleCN: 一个相关的名词指可见的形状本身。

items.example: Latin forms the adjective for what exists as a pattern.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语构成形容词，指作为模式而存在的东西。

items.meaning: the best possible, or existing only as a model
items.meaningCN: 理想的；只作为典范存在的
items.example: English takes the adjective from French.
items.exampleCN: 英语从法语接收这个形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective from the noun.
It forms idealism, a system of thought.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 idealism，即一套思想体系。

items.example: It forms idealist, a person who holds to ideals.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 idealist，即坚持理想的人。

items.example: It forms idealize, to treat something as perfect.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 idealize，即把某物看得完美。

items.example: It forms the adverb that sets out the best case.
items.exampleCN: 它构成摆出最佳情形的副词。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「形相、所见」经拉丁与法语借入，义为「观念」
由观念名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「理想的」
由理想形容词加表示学说体系的名词尾构成，义为「理想主义」
由理想形容词加表示人的名词尾构成，义为「理想主义者」
由理想形容词加动词词尾构成，义为「把……理想化」

definition_zh: 咨询；请教；查阅
definition_en: to ask someone for advice, or to look something up for information
core_image: 一个人拿着地图，向路边的老人问路
scene: 出发前，他先给当地的朋友打了个电话。 You should consult a doctor before taking the pills.
sceneCN: 这里 consult 指「咨询、请教」（第 1 个义项：向人求取意见）；句意是吃药前你应当咨询医生。

senses.title: Ask for advice
senses.definition: to ask a person with knowledge for their opinion
senses.definitionCN: 向有知识的人征询意见
senses.example: Consult a doctor if the pain continues.
senses.exampleCN: 如果疼痛持续，请咨询医生。
senses.why: No one carries every answer, so some answers must be asked for.
senses.whyCN: 没人能带着所有答案，所以有些答案必须去问。

senses.title: Look it up
senses.definition: to search a book or record for information
senses.definitionCN: 在书本或记录中查找信息
senses.example: He consulted the map before setting out.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前他查了地图。
senses.why: A dictionary is advice that has been waiting quietly.
senses.whyCN: 词典是一份安静等候着的意见。

senses.title: Talk it over
senses.definition: to discuss something with others before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 做决定前与他人一起讨论
senses.example: The mayor consulted with local groups.
senses.exampleCN: 市长与当地团体进行了商议。
senses.why: A decision shared before it is made is harder to resent later.
senses.whyCN: 做决定前先商量，日后就不容易招怨。

intro.en: Consult comes from Latin consultare, to take counsel, a frequent form of consulere, to gather and deliberate.
intro.cn: consult 来自拉丁语 consultare，意为商议，是 consulere（聚集商议）的反复形式。

items.en: Consulere meant to gather people to deliberate.
items.cn: consulere 意为召集众人商议。

items.en: It also meant to look after the interests of someone.
items.cn: 它也指照看某人的利益。

items.en: Consultare repeated the act of asking for counsel.
items.cn: consultare 表示反复地征询意见。

items.en: French consulter carried the word into advice and books.
items.cn: 法语 consulter 把这个词带到求教与查书。

items.en: English consult meant to seek advice from a person.
items.cn: 英语 consult 指向人求教。

items.en: It now also covers checking a map, a file or a record.
items.cn: 如今它也指查地图、查档案或查记录。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin counsel base, and the meaning group names other verbs for seeking information or advice.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的商议词基，近义组列出其他表示求取信息或意见的动词。

entries.definition: an expert who gives professional advice
a meeting to seek advice or decide together
to speak to someone in a rude way
to say that you want information or help
to discuss something with others
to look at a source for information

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a question put to a stranger, then move to a page searched for a fact and to a table where people talk it over.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从向陌生人提出的问题开始，再到为找一个事实而翻开的书页，最后到众人商谈的桌子。

normal.en: Con- is together and sult is gather, so consult is gathering advice from someone.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sult 是聚集，consult 就是把意见聚拢过来。

normal.en: A map held open at a crossroads: that is consult.
normal.cn: 在十字路口摊开一张地图，那就是查阅。

normal.en: Ask before you act, and you have consulted.
normal.cn: 动手之前先问过，你就已经咨询过了。

normal.en: A dictionary is a quiet consultant on the shelf.
normal.cn: 词典是书架上一位安静的顾问。

normal.en: Two heads talking before one hand moves.
normal.cn: 两只脑袋先商量，一只手再行动。

abstract.en: Picture a finger running down a list of names.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指顺着一列名字往下滑。

abstract.en: Picture a phone held to an ear in a hallway.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊里贴着耳朵的手机。

abstract.en: Picture a book opened flat beside a cold cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊平的书旁边放着一杯凉茶。

examples.en: You had better consult a specialist about the pain.
examples.cn: 关于这处疼痛，你最好咨询专科医生。

examples.en: She consulted the dictionary for the exact meaning.
examples.cn: 她查词典确认准确含义。

examples.en: The committee consulted with parents before changing the rules.
examples.cn: 委员会在修改规定前与家长进行了商议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consult 记成 con（一起）加 sult（聚集）：把懂行的人聚到一起问个明白，就是咨询、请教。

root: 源自拉丁语 consultare（反复商议），本义是聚在一起商量，后指向人请教、查阅资料与共同商议。

sensesIntro.en: From a question put to an expert, to a fact hunted down in a book, and to people sitting together before a decision.
sensesIntro.cn: 从向专家提出的问题，到书里找出的一个事实，最后到决定前坐在一起的众人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone holding a map open, asking a stranger the way.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人摊开地图，向陌生人问路。

branches.en: The first sense is a question handed to someone who knows more.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把问题交给懂得更多的人。

branches.en: The second sense asks a page instead of a person.
branches.cn: 第二个义项问的是一页纸，而不是一个人。

branches.en: The third sense puts several voices around one table.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把几个声音放到同一张桌子旁。

branches.en: Both senses go looking for knowledge outside the self.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是到自己之外去寻找知识。

branches.en: Advice and discussion both end in a better informed choice.
branches.cn: 请教与商议都以更知情的选择收尾。

intro.en: Consult is built on Latin con-, together, plus consulere, to gather and deliberate.
intro.cn: consult 由拉丁语 con-（一起）与 consulere（聚集商议）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin counsel base consult- also appears in consultant, consultation and consultative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的商议词基 consult- 也出现在 consultant、consultation 与 consultative 中。

items.example: Consult the guide before you climb.

items.meaning: a person who gives expert advice
items.exampleCN: 他们请了一位税务顾问。

items.meaning: a meeting held to seek advice
items.exampleCN: 这次咨询持续了一小时。

items.example: The group has a consultative role.
items.exampleCN: 这个小组只承担咨询角色。

items.meaning: an official who looks after citizens abroad
items.meaningCN: 在海外照看本国公民的官员
items.example: The consul helped them replace their papers.
items.exampleCN: 领事帮他们补办了证件。

items.meaning: to leap at someone with rude words
items.example: He did not mean to insult her.
She sought counsel from an old teacher.

items.meaning: able to be looked up or asked
items.example: The archive is open and consultable.
items.exampleCN: 这批档案开放且可供查阅。

definition_zh: 闲暇；空闲时间；休闲活动；悠闲；休闲（作定语）
definition_en: time free from work or duties, the activities that fill it, and the relaxed manner that such time allows
core_image: 安静午后的一张空藤椅，旁边放着一杯还冒着热气的茶
scene: 周末的午后，会议与邮件都停了，阳台上的藤椅空着，等一个人端着茶坐下来。 Long afternoons of leisure left him free to read whatever he liked.
sceneCN: 这里是「空闲时间」（第 1 个义项：不必工作的自由时间）；句意为漫长的闲暇午后让他能随心读书。图中可辨识物件：阳台藤椅、茶杯、翻开的书。

pos.zh: 闲暇；空闲时间；休闲活动

derivatives.zh: 由 leisure 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「从容的；不慌不忙的」
由 leisure 加 -ed 构成，义为「有大量空闲时间的」
由 leisure 与 wear 复合而成，义为「休闲服饰」

senses.title: Time free from work or duty
senses.definition: time when you are not working and may choose for yourself what to do
senses.definitionCN: 不必工作、可以由自己决定做什么的那段时间
senses.example: She has little leisure during the exam season.
senses.exampleCN: 考试季她几乎没有空闲时间。
senses.why: Latin licere meant to be permitted, so leisure began as permitted time, the hours no duty can claim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licere 意为「被允许」，leisure 最初指被允许自由支配的时间，也就是没有职责占用的那几个小时。

senses.title: Activities enjoyed in that free time
senses.definition: the things people choose to do for pleasure when work is finished
senses.definitionCN: 工作结束后人们为了愉快而选择去做的事情
senses.example: Reading and cycling are his favourite forms of leisure.
senses.exampleCN: 读书和骑车是他最喜欢的休闲方式。
senses.why: Once free hours exist they must be filled, so the word slides from the empty time to the chosen activity that occupies it.
senses.whyCN: 空闲的小时一旦存在，就必然被填满，于是词义从「空白的时间」滑向占用这段时间的自选活动。

senses.title: An unhurried, easy manner
senses.definition: a relaxed way of acting, with no pressure of time and no need to rush
senses.definitionCN: 不受时间压迫、不必赶的轻松做事方式
senses.example: He answered the questions at his leisure.
senses.exampleCN: 他不慌不忙地回答了问题。
senses.why: Time that carries no deadline produces a manner without hurry, so at leisure comes to describe the calm inside the free hours.
senses.whyCN: 没有截止期限的时间会带来不赶的态度，于是 at leisure 用来描述空闲时间里那种从容的心境。

senses.title: Placed before a noun: made for free time
senses.definition: used in front of another noun for places, clothes or industries serving people at leisure
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，指服务于闲暇之人的场所、衣物或产业
senses.example: The town opened a new leisure centre last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇去年春天新开了一家休闲中心。
senses.why: A noun naming free time easily turns into a label on the things built for it, which is why leisure attaches to centres, wear and whole industries.
senses.whyCN: 表示空闲时间的名词很容易变成「为其建造之物」的标签，所以 leisure 能贴在中心、服饰乃至整个产业前面。

intro.en: Leisure comes from a Latin verb of permission and reached English through French, still carrying the idea of hours that nobody else can claim.
intro.cn: leisure 源自拉丁语中表示「允许」的动词，经法语进入英语，至今仍带着「无人能占用的时间」这层意思。

items.en: Licere meant to be allowed or permitted, and it named what a person was free to do.
items.cn: licere 意为「被允许、获准」，指一个人可以自由去做的事。

items.en: Its noun licentia named permission or freedom, the state of being allowed.
items.cn: 其名词 licentia 表示许可或自由，即「获准的状态」。

items.en: Old French shaped the verb as leisir, which meant both to be allowed and the free time that followed.
items.cn: 古法语把动词写作 leisir，既表示「被允许」，也指随之而来的空闲时间。

items.en: Middle English used leisir, later spelled leisure, for time at one's own disposal.
items.cn: 中古英语用 leisir（后写作 leisure）指由自己支配的时间。

items.en: Modern English keeps leisure for free time and extends it to leisure activities, leisure wear and the leisure industry.
items.cn: 现代英语用 leisure 指空闲时间，并扩展到休闲活动、休闲服饰与休闲产业。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same Latin verb of permission; the near-meaning group collects words for spare hours and rest.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「允许」动词上的派生形式；近义组收表示空闲与休息的词。

entries.definition: Acting or moving without hurry.
Having plenty of free time, usually through wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 有大量空闲时间的，通常因富裕。

entries.definition: Allowed by law; the opposite of illicit.
entries.definitionCN: 法律允许的；illicit 的反义词。

entries.definition: Official permission to do something, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 官方许可，来自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Time left over after work or duties.
entries.definitionCN: 工作或职责之外剩下的时间。

entries.definition: Resting and letting tension go.
Activities done for enjoyment outside work.
entries.definitionCN: 工作之外为消遣而做的活动。

entries.definition: The state of not working, often with a hint of disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 不做事的状态，常带一点贬义。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for being allowed, and its family keeps returning to permission, free hours and the easy manner they produce.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「获准」的拉丁动词上，同族词反复回到许可、空闲时间以及由此产生的从容态度。

normal.en: Licere in Latin means to be allowed, so leisure is time you are permitted to spend as you wish.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 licere 意为被允许，所以 leisure 是可以随自己支配的获准时间。

normal.en: Old French leisir dropped its verb ending and became leisure, keeping both the permission and the free hours.
normal.cn: 古法语 leisir 去掉动词词尾后成为 leisure，同时保留「许可」和「空闲时间」两层意思。

normal.en: Leisurely adds -ly to leisure, describing the unhurried manner of someone inside free time.
normal.cn: leisurely 在 leisure 后加 -ly，形容人处在空闲时间里的从容样子。

normal.en: Leisure wear joins leisure to wear, clothing for hours when no uniform is required.
normal.cn: leisure wear 把 leisure 与 wear 连起来，指不必穿制服的时段所穿的衣服。

normal.en: The phrase is at leisure, not in leisure, because you sit inside your own free time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 at leisure 而不是 in leisure，因为人坐在自己的空闲时间里。

abstract.en: A word that first meant permission reminds us that free time is not empty space but time granted to us.
abstract.cn: 一个最初表示「许可」的词提醒人：空闲不是空白，而是被准许使用的时光。

abstract.en: Leisure links restful hours with a calm manner, suggesting that how we spend time shapes how we carry ourselves.
abstract.cn: leisure 把休息的时段与从容的态度连在一起，说明怎样花时间会影响人的举止。

abstract.en: When leisure becomes an industry, the very hours once free now have goods built around them.
abstract.cn: 当 leisure 变成一种产业，原本自由的时段周围就长出了专门为它制造的商品。

examples.en: She has little leisure during the exam season.
examples.cn: 考试季她几乎没有空闲时间。

examples.en: Reading and cycling are his favourite forms of leisure.
examples.cn: 读书和骑车是他最喜欢的休闲方式。

examples.en: He answered the questions at his leisure.
examples.cn: 他不慌不忙地回答了问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来这儿」——有空的时候，来这儿坐坐；记住 leisure 是空闲、闲暇。

root: 拉丁语 licere（被允许）→ 拉丁名词 licentia（许可）→ 古法语 leisir（获准的空闲）→ 中古英语 leisure；同族词多与「许可、自由」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is permitted free time; from it grow the activities that fill those hours, the unhurried manner they allow, and the attributive use for things made for them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被允许自由支配的时间」；由此长出填充这些时间的活动、随之而来的从容态度，以及修饰休闲事物的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair on a quiet afternoon, waiting for someone with nowhere else to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：安静午后的一张空椅子，等一个无别处可去的人。

branches.en: a clock with no appointment marked on it
branches.cn: 一只没有记下任何约会的钟

branches.en: a bicycle leaning against a park bench
branches.cn: 靠在公园长椅上的自行车

branches.en: a town building named after free hours
branches.cn: 以闲暇时光命名的小镇建筑

branches.en: a man answering slowly, with no deadline
branches.cn: 不赶时间、从容作答的人

branches.en: a shop window full of clothes for weekends
branches.cn: 橱窗里摆满周末穿的休闲衣

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of permission and its noun, reshaped by French, then extended by English suffixes into a manner and a garment.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示许可的拉丁动词及其名词支撑，经法语改写，再由英语后缀扩展出「态度」和「衣物」。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 观察；注意到；作科学观测；评论说；遵守；庆祝（节日或仪式）
definition_en: to watch something carefully, to notice, to make a scientific observation, to remark, or to keep a rule or mark a day
core_image: 山顶观测台上，一个人屏住呼吸把望远镜对准同一颗星，每隔一刻钟记下一次位置
scene: 山顶的观测台上，一个人每隔一刻钟记录一次那颗星的位置，直到云层压过来。 Astronomers observe the same star for months to fix its distance.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：为获取信息而长时间仔细观看；句意为天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、记录表、计时器、星图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观察；注意到；观测；评论；遵守；庆祝

senses.title: To watch with full attention
senses.definition: to watch someone or something closely over time in order to learn how it behaves
senses.definitionCN: 为弄清某人或某物的行为而长时间仔细观看
senses.example: Astronomers observe the same star for months to fix its distance.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to watch over and heed, so sustained attention rather than a glance is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为看守并留心，因此持续注意而非一眼扫过，是最古老的一层。

senses.title: To notice
senses.definition: to see or become aware of something, often without looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 看见或意识到某物，往往并非刻意寻找
senses.example: I observed a crack in the glass before it fell.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃掉落之前，我就注意到上面有道裂痕。
senses.why: Attention can be caught as well as directed, so the same verb covers the moment something enters the eye.
senses.whyCN: 注意力既能被引导也能被抓住，因此同一个动词也覆盖某物进入视野的那一刻。

senses.title: To measure in a study
senses.definition: to record a phenomenon under controlled conditions as part of scientific work
senses.definitionCN: 作为科研工作的一部分，在受控条件下记录一种现象
senses.example: The team observe the cells every six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每六小时观察一次这些细胞。
senses.why: Measurement begins with watching, and science made the watching formal by giving it conditions and records.
senses.whyCN: 测量始于观看，而科学通过附加条件与记录，把观看变得正式。

senses.title: To remark
senses.definition: to say something as a comment on what has been noticed
senses.definitionCN: 就注意到的事情说一句话作为评论
senses.example: The reviewer observed that the sample was too small.
senses.exampleCN: 评审人评论说样本太小。
senses.why: A remark is often the spoken form of something noticed, so the verb moved from the eye to the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 评论常常是「注意到的东西」的口头形式，这个动词于是从眼睛移到了嘴。

senses.title: To keep a rule
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a law, rule, custom or promise
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、规则、习俗或承诺行事
senses.example: Drivers must observe the speed limit near the school.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在学校附近必须遵守限速。
senses.why: To observe a rule is to keep watch over yourself, the same inward attention the Latin verb first described.
senses.whyCN: 遵守规则就是看住自己，正是那个拉丁动词最初描述的内在注意。

senses.title: To mark a day or rite
senses.definition: to celebrate or carry out a day, festival or ceremony in the proper way
senses.definitionCN: 以适当方式庆祝某个日子、节日或举行仪式
senses.example: The village observes the harvest festival every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子每年秋天都过丰收节。
senses.why: A custom is kept by being performed on its day, so the sense of keeping widened to the act of celebration.
senses.whyCN: 习俗靠在其日子被践行而得以保持，因此「持守」之义扩展到庆祝行为。

senses.title: To keep someone under watch
senses.definition: to watch a person or place secretly, especially as part of an investigation
senses.definitionCN: 暗中监视某人或某地，尤作为调查的一部分
senses.example: Police observe the house from a van across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在街对面的货车里监视那栋房子。
senses.why: The same careful watching turns into surveillance when the watcher does not wish to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 当观看者不愿被看见，同样的仔细观看就变成了监视。

senses.title: To watch without interfering
senses.definition: in research, to study behaviour while taking no part that would change it
senses.definitionCN: 在研究中研究行为，同时不介入以免改变它
senses.example: The psychologist observes the class from the back of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学家在教室后排观察这个班。
senses.why: If the observer changes what is observed, the record is spoiled, so method demands watching with hands off.
senses.whyCN: 观察者若改变了被观察对象，记录就毁了，因此方法要求袖手旁观。

intro.en: Observe comes from Latin observare 'to watch over, heed', built on ob- 'over, before' and servare 'to keep, preserve'. The rule-keeping and celebration senses came through religious usage, and the scientific sense settled in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: observe 来自拉丁语 observare「看守、留心」，由 ob-「在……之上、在……之前」与 servare「保持、守护」构成。守规与庆祝两义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义则在十七世纪定型。

items.en: Servare meant to keep safe, preserve or watch over, and it stands behind preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.cn: servare 意为保全、守护、看守，preserve、reserve 与 conserve 都出自它。

items.en: The similar-looking servire meant to serve, and it gave servant and service; the two Latin verbs are different words.
items.cn: 形近的 servire 意为服侍，产生了 servant 与 service；这两个拉丁动词是不同的词。

items.en: Ob- plus servare made a verb for watching over something and attending to it, with attention as the core.
items.cn: ob- 加 servare 构成「看守并留心某物」的动词，核心在注意。

items.en: Old French observer carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of keeping a rule.
items.cn: 古法语 observer 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初意为遵守规则。

items.en: Observing the Sabbath and observing a fast fixed the senses of keeping a custom and of celebrating its day.
items.cn: 守安息日、守斋期固定了「持守习俗」与「在其日子举行」两种含义。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy made observe a technical word for recorded watching, and observatory and observer followed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的天文学把 observe 变成指「有记录观看」的技术词，天文台与观察者二词随之而来。

note.en: The first group shares the keeping root or looks close; the second group names ways of watching.
note.cn: 第一组共享「守护」词根或形近；第二组是各种「看」的方式。

entries.definition: The act or result of watching and recording.
entries.definitionCN: 观看并记录的行为或结果。

entries.definition: The person who watches, including the mere onlooker.
entries.definitionCN: 进行观看的人，也包括单纯旁观者。

entries.definition: Quick to notice details; also careful in keeping rules.
entries.definitionCN: 善于察觉细节的；也指守规谨慎的。

entries.definition: The keeping of a rule or rite, not the act of looking.
entries.definitionCN: 对规则或仪式的遵行，而非观看动作。

entries.definition: A building fitted for watching the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 为观测天空而建的场所。

entries.definition: To keep safe from harm, from the same keeping verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 使免受损害，同一守护动词加不同前缀。

entries.definition: Work done for others, from servire 'to serve', not from servare.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人所做的工作，出自表示「服侍」的拉丁动词，而非表示「守护」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for looking at something over a period, with less formality.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指持续一段时间看某物，正式程度较低。

entries.definition: To become aware of something, without the suggestion of sustained study.
entries.definitionCN: 意识到某物，不含持续研究的意味。

entries.definition: To keep a continuous check, often with instruments.
To look over a whole area or group, often to record its state.
entries.definitionCN: 遍览整个区域或群体，常为记录其状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the keeping verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of rules, rites and research.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「守护」动词、真实同族词，以及规则、仪式与研究里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin servare meant to keep safe, so observe is literally to keep watch over something.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 servare 意为保全，observe 字面就是看住某物。

normal.en: The family runs observe, observation, observer, observant and observatory.
normal.cn: 同族词有 observe、observation、observer、observant 与 observatory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: observe a rule, observe a holiday, observe that.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：遵守规则、庆祝节日、评论说。

normal.en: Preserve and reserve share the keeping verb, while servant and service come from the serving verb.
normal.cn: preserve 与 reserve 共享「守护」动词，而 servant 与 service 出自「服侍」动词。

normal.en: An observatory is a building named for the watching, not for the stars.
normal.cn: 天文台是因「观看」而得名，而非因星星。

abstract.en: To observe a rule is to watch yourself as closely as you watch others.
abstract.cn: 遵守规则，就是像看别人那样看住自己。

abstract.en: The observer who changes the scene has already lost the thing worth recording.
abstract.cn: 改变场景的观察者，已经失去了值得记录的东西。

abstract.en: Attention is the whole word: watch, keep, and do not blink.
abstract.cn: 整个词就是注意：看着、守着、别眨眼。

examples.en: She observed the birds from the hide without making a sound.
examples.cn: 她藏在小棚里观察鸟，没有发出一点声音。

examples.en: Every driver must observe the signs at the crossing.
examples.cn: 每位司机在路口都必须遵守标志。

examples.en: The committee observed a minute of silence for the victims.
examples.cn: 委员会为遇难者默哀一分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧布泽夫」——守在旁边盯住不放，看到什么就记下来：观察

root: 拉丁语 servare「保全、守护」→ observare「看守、留心」（ob- 加 servare）；经古法语 observer 进入英语。守规与庆祝义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义在十七世纪定型。注意与 servire「服侍」并非同词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pair of watching eyes: sustained attention, a sudden notice, a measured record, a spoken remark, a rule kept, a festival marked, a house watched in secret, and a class studied without interference.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一双观看的眼睛：持续注意、忽然察觉、有记录的测量、口头评论、被遵守的规则、被举行的节日、被暗中监视的房子，以及不干预地研究的课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: on a hilltop a watcher holds a telescope on one star and writes its position every quarter hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：山顶的观测者用望远镜对准一颗星，每刻钟记下它的位置。

branches.en: THE EYES: watching for a long time, and catching something in passing.
branches.cn: 那双眼：长时间的看，与路过时捕捉到什么。

branches.en: THE RECORD: cells counted every six hours, a class watched from the back without interference.
branches.cn: 记录：每六小时数一次细胞，在教室后排不干预地观察一个班。

branches.en: THE MOUTH: a note spoken aloud after the eyes have done their work.
branches.cn: 嘴：眼睛做完活之后，说出口的一句评论。

branches.en: THE KEPT RULE: attention turned inward, so that the driver watches himself.
branches.cn: 被守的规则：注意转向内部，司机看住自己。

branches.en: THE MARKED DAY AND THE SECRET WATCH: a rite performed on its date, a house watched from a van.
branches.cn: 被举行的日子与暗中监视：在正日子举行的仪式，与从货车里盯住的房子。

intro.en: Observe is a Latin verb of keeping watch, and its family split off from the separate verb meaning to serve.
intro.cn: observe 是一个表示看守的拉丁动词，其词族与另一个意为服侍的动词分道而行。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is servare, ob-, observare and the noun observatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 servare、ob-、observare 与名词 observatio。

items.example: The verb keeps the image of a guard at a post.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留着岗哨看守的意象。

items.example: It also gives preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「保存」「保留」与「保护」三词的来源。

items.example: It gives servant and service, and is not the root here.
items.exampleCN: 它产生「仆人」与「服务」两词，不是这里的词根。

items.example: It adds the idea of watching over something.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「看住某物」的意思。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The noun names both the act and its record.
items.exampleCN: 名词兼指行为与其记录。

items.example: The agent noun includes the mere onlooker.
items.exampleCN: 施事名词包括单纯旁观者。

items.example: The adjective also means careful in keeping rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也指守规谨慎的。

items.meaning: the keeping of a rule or rite

items.example: The suffix names a place of work.

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb servare (serv-, servatum; to keep)
latinEntries.example: Latin servare means to keep or preserve.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 servare 意为保持、守护。

latinEntries.example: Latin ob- appears in obicere, to throw against.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ob- 见于 obicere（扔向对面）。

latinEntries.example: Latin observare means to watch over, to heed.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observare 意为看守、留意。

latinEntries.example: Latin observatio means a watching or a noting.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observatio 意为观看、记录。

definition_zh: 天赋；才能；人才
definition_en: a natural ability to do something well, or people who have such ability
core_image: 天平一端称出沉甸甸的分量
scene: 教练一眼就看出这个少年身上有天赋。 The coach saw at once that the boy had talent.
sceneCN: 这里 talent 是「天赋、才能」（第 1 个义项）；句意：教练一眼就看出这个少年身上有天赋。

senses.title: A natural ability
senses.definition: a natural ability to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 把某件事做好的天生能力
senses.example: The coach saw at once that the boy had talent.
senses.exampleCN: 教练一眼就看出这个少年有天赋。
senses.why: A talent was once a weighed amount of metal, so ability was pictured as something measured out.
senses.whyCN: talent 原指称量出的一笔金属，于是才能被想象成天生「分到」的分量。

senses.title: People with ability
senses.definition: people who are good at something, considered as a group
senses.definitionCN: 被作为一个群体看待的有才干的人
senses.example: The company is looking for young talent.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在寻找年轻人才。
senses.why: The ability was transferred to the people who carry it.
senses.whyCN: 「才能」这一抽象物被转移到拥有它的人身上。

intro.en: Talent began as a unit of weight and value before it meant a gift.
intro.cn: talent 最初是重量与价值的单位，后来才表示天赋。

items.en: Talanton meant a balance and a weighed sum.
items.cn: talanton 意为天平与称出的数额。

items.en: Talentum kept the sense of a weight of money.
items.cn: talentum 保留了「一笔重量的钱」之义。

items.en: Talenta appeared in biblical parables of entrusted money.
items.cn: talenta 出现在受托钱财的圣经比喻中。

items.en: Talent came to mean a God-given ability.
items.cn: talent 转而表示上天赋予的能力。

items.en: It now means natural ability and able people.
items.cn: 现代英语中指天赋与有才能的人。

note.en: Talent is compared with look-alike forms and with words for ability.
note.cn: 把 talent 与形近形式以及表示能力的词作对比。

abstract.en: Ability arrives as if weighed and handed over.
abstract.cn: 才能仿佛被称量好再交到手里。

abstract.en: A scale became a gift.
abstract.cn: 一架天平变成了礼物。

abstract.en: What is measured out can still grow.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太能」——「太能」干的人，就是身上有天赋的人。

root: 希腊语 talanton（天平、称出的重量）经拉丁语 talentum 进入英语，由「一笔钱财」转为「天赋」。

sensesIntro.en: From a weighed sum of money, talent moved to an inborn ability and then to able people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从称出的一笔钱，talent 转向天生的能力，再转向有才能的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of scales weighing out a share.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平称出一份分量。

branches.en: Ability inherits the image of a measured share.
branches.cn: 才能继承了「分得的一份」这一形象。

branches.en: The gift stands for the gifted.
branches.cn: 「天赋」转指拥有天赋的人。

branches.en: One word holds both the gift and its bearers.
branches.cn: 一个词同时容纳天赋与拥有者。

branches.en: The scale suggests something given, not earned.
branches.cn: 天平暗示才能是被赋予而非赚来的。

branches.en: A pool of talent is a pool of people.
branches.cn: 人才储备就是一群人的储备。

intro.en: Talent has a tight family of adjectives and a vivid root history.
intro.cn: talent 有一个紧凑的形容词词族和生动的词根史。

latinIntro.en: Latin talentum, from Greek talanton, means a balance and a weighed sum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 talentum（源自希腊语 talanton）意为天平与称出的数额。

items.example: Talentum meant a sum of money.

latinEntries.example: Talentum meant a sum of money.

definition_zh: 感激的；感谢的
definition_en: feeling thankful for something
core_image: 一个人双手接过礼物，眼里带着谢意
scene: 她感激朋友在她困难时的帮助。 She was grateful to her friend for the help.
sceneCN: 这里 grateful 是「感激的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她感激朋友在她困难时的帮助。

senses.title: Feeling thankful
senses.definition: feeling thankful for something received
senses.definitionCN: 因得到帮助而心怀感谢的
senses.example: She was grateful to her friend for the help.
senses.exampleCN: 她感激朋友在她困难时的帮助。
senses.why: Thankful feeling is the core modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 心怀感谢是现代最核心的用法。

senses.title: Expressing thanks
senses.definition: showing or expressing thanks
senses.definitionCN: 表达谢意的
senses.example: He sent a grateful letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他寄了一封感谢信。
senses.why: The feeling is turned into words and gifts.
senses.whyCN: 把感激之情化为文字与礼物。

senses.title: Pleasing
senses.definition: pleasant or welcome, in older use
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中指令人愉快、受欢迎的
senses.example: The grateful shade saved us from the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 宜人的树荫让我们免于日晒。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply pleasing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「令人愉快的」。

intro.en: Grateful comes from Latin gratus, pleasing or thankful.
intro.cn: grateful 来自拉丁语 gratus，意为令人愉快的或感激的。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing or thankful.
items.cn: gratus 意为令人愉快的或感激的。

items.en: Gratia meant grace, thanks, and favor.
items.cn: gratia 意为恩惠、感谢与好感。

items.en: Gratus grew the sense of feeling thanks.
items.cn: gratus 发展出心怀感谢之义。

items.en: Grateful entered English as thankful.
items.cn: grateful 以「感激的」之义进入英语。

items.en: It also kept the older sense of pleasing.
items.cn: 它也保留了较古老的「令人愉快」之义。

note.en: Grateful is compared with look-alike words and words for thanks.
note.cn: 把 grateful 与形近词以及表示感谢的词作比较。

entries.definition: very large or good
to rub into small pieces
the feeling of thanks
feeling thanks
showing that you value something
thankful for a favor

normalIntro.en: Grateful is the heart saying thank you.
normalIntro.cn: grateful 就是心里在说谢谢。

normal.en: I am grateful for your help.
normal.cn: 我很感激你的帮助。

normal.en: She felt grateful to the doctor.
normal.cn: 她对医生心怀感激。

normal.en: We are grateful for the rain.
normal.cn: 我们感谢这场雨。

normal.en: He wrote a grateful note.
normal.cn: 他写了一张感谢便条。

normal.en: They were grateful to be safe.
normal.cn: 他们庆幸自己平安。

abstract.en: Gratitude turns what we have into enough.
abstract.cn: 感激，让已有的变成足够。

abstract.en: A grateful heart keeps a light on.
abstract.cn: 感激的心，总留着一盏灯。

abstract.en: Small kindnesses are remembered longest.
abstract.cn: 微小的善意，记得最久。

examples.en: She was grateful to her friend for the help.
examples.cn: 她感激朋友在她困难时的帮助。

examples.en: He sent a grateful letter.
examples.cn: 他寄了一封感谢信。

examples.en: The grateful shade saved us from the sun.
examples.cn: 宜人的树荫让我们免于日晒。

dict_mnemonic.text: grateful 与 gratitude（感激）同根，词根意为「令人愉快的、感激的」；be grateful for 是对事感激，be grateful to 是对人感激；注意与 great（伟大的）区分。

root: 来自拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快的、感激的），经中古英语进入英语，核心义由「讨人喜欢的」转为「心怀感谢的」。

sensesIntro.en: Grateful means feeling thankful, expressing thanks, or, in older use, pleasing.
sensesIntro.cn: grateful 指心怀感激、表达谢意，或旧用法中的令人愉快。

core.en: A heart warmed by a received kindness.
core.cn: 因受惠而暖起来的心。

branches.en: A hand rests on the heart.
branches.cn: 一只手按在胸口。

branches.en: A short letter says more than it must.
branches.cn: 一封短信，说的比该说的多。

branches.en: Cool shade welcomes a tired walker.
branches.cn: 凉爽的树荫迎接疲惫的行人。

branches.en: Feeling and words belong together.
branches.cn: 心情与言语，本该成对。

branches.en: Thanks can be spoken or simply felt as comfort.
branches.cn: 谢意可以说出口，也可以化作舒适。

intro.en: Grateful forms comparison, adverbs, and nouns.
intro.cn: grateful 构成比较级、副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is gratus, pleasing or thankful.

definition_zh: 全面的；综合的；广泛的；综合中学
definition_en: including everything that is needed or relevant
core_image: 一张摊满整张桌面的大地图，把每条小路都画上
scene: 报告把每个环节都列了进去，一页也没漏。 The report gives a comprehensive review of the whole project.
sceneCN: 这里 comprehensive 指「全面的」（第 1 个义项：涵盖所有部分）；句意是这份报告对整个项目做了全面回顾。

senses.title: Covering every part
senses.definition: including all or nearly all the parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 包含某事物的全部或几乎全部部分
senses.example: The book offers a comprehensive guide to the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书提供了一份全面的城市指南。
senses.why: A guide is called comprehensive when nothing important has been left out.
senses.whyCN: 当重要内容一样也没漏时，指南才被称为全面的。

senses.title: Wide in scope
senses.definition: broad enough to include many different things
senses.definitionCN: 范围足够广，能包含许多不同事物
senses.example: The law had a comprehensive effect on trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法律对贸易产生了广泛影响。
senses.why: Scope is breadth rather than depth, and comprehensive words stretch wide.
senses.whyCN: 范围讲的是广度而非深度，comprehensive 正是向四周铺开。

senses.title: A school for all abilities
senses.definition: in Britain, a secondary school for pupils of all abilities
senses.definitionCN: 在英国，招收各种能力学生的中学
senses.example: She went to the local comprehensive.
senses.exampleCN: 她上了当地的综合中学。
senses.why: The school takes in every kind of pupil, so it is comprehensive in people too.
senses.whyCN: 这所学校接纳各种学生，所以在人的意义上也是全面的。

intro.en: Comprehensive comes from Latin comprehendere, to seize or grasp, and first meant having the power to grasp everything.
intro.cn: comprehensive 来自拉丁语 comprehendere（抓住），最初指有能力把一切都抓住。

items.en: Comprehendere meant to seize or to take in completely.
items.cn: comprehendere 意为抓住或完整地纳入。

items.en: Comprehensivus described something that could take in all.
items.cn: comprehensivus 描述能纳入一切的东西。

items.en: French compréhensif kept the idea of wide grasp.
items.cn: 法语 compréhensif 保留了广泛把握的意思。

items.en: English comprehensive first meant including much in a small space.
items.cn: 英语 comprehensive 最初指在小篇幅内包含很多内容。

items.en: It grew to describe reports, insurance and schools.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到描述报告、保险与学校。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words sharing the shape of comprehensive, and the meaning group names other words for covering a whole.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 comprehensive 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示覆盖整体的词。

the ability to understand

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a map that fills the whole table, then move to reports and to a school open to all.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张铺满整桌的地图开始，再走到报告与向所有人开放的学校。

normal.en: Comprehend is to grasp, so comprehensive means able to grasp everything.
normal.cn: comprehend 是抓住，所以 comprehensive 就是能把一切抓住。

normal.en: A comprehensive review checks every room, not just the hall.

normal.en: Comprehensive insurance covers many kinds of damage at once.

normal.en: A comprehensive school takes pupils of every ability.

normal.en: Comprehensive and comprehensible differ: one covers all, one is easy to grasp.
normal.cn: comprehensive 与 comprehensible 不同：一个覆盖全部，一个容易理解。

abstract.en: Picture a map so large that no road is missing.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图大得没有一条路被漏掉。

abstract.en: Picture a checklist with every box already ticked.
abstract.cn: 想象一张清单，每个格子都已打勾。

abstract.en: Picture one net thrown over an entire field.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网罩住整片田野。

examples.en: The committee ordered a comprehensive review of the budget.
examples.cn: 委员会要求对预算进行全面审查。

examples.en: This dictionary aims to be comprehensive.
examples.cn: 这部词典力求全面。

examples.en: He attended a comprehensive in the north of the city.
examples.cn: 他在城北的一所综合中学就读。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comprehensive 记成 com（一起）加 prehend（抓住）：把所有部分一起抓住，就是全面的。

root: 源自拉丁语 comprehendere（com 一起 + prehendere 抓住），本义是全部抓住，后引申为全面的、广泛的，并指招收各类学生的综合中学。

sensesIntro.en: From all parts of a thing, to a wide reach, and finally to a school that takes in every kind of pupil.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一件事的所有部分，到宽广的范围，最后到接纳各类学生的学校。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map spread over the whole table, with every small road drawn in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张铺满整桌的地图，连每条小路都画上了。

branches.en: Completeness of parts is the central sense.
branches.cn: 部分的完整是核心义项。

branches.en: Width of range is completeness stretched sideways.
branches.cn: 范围的宽广，是完整性向两侧铺开。

branches.en: A school becomes comprehensive by including all pupils.
branches.cn: 学校因接纳所有学生而变得 comprehensive。

branches.en: Both senses answer the question of what has been left out.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在回答漏掉了什么。

branches.en: A full report and a full school both refuse to exclude.
branches.cn: 完整的报告与完整的学校都拒绝排除。

intro.en: Comprehensive is built on Latin com-, together, plus prehendere, to seize, with the adjective ending -ive.
intro.cn: comprehensive 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、prehendere（抓住）与形容词词尾 -ive 构成。

latinIntro.en: The same base gives comprehension, comprehend and comprehensible.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个词基还给出 comprehension、comprehend 与 comprehensible。

items.exampleCN: 他们写了一份全面的计划。

items.example: The team reviewed the data comprehensively.
items.exampleCN: 团队全面地审查了数据。

items.example: The comprehensiveness of the index impressed us.

items.example: Her answer was short and comprehensible.
