items.exampleCN: 编辑检查每一页的可理解性。

definition_zh: 劈开；分裂；分担；绝交；（名）裂缝；分歧
definition_en: to divide something into two or more parts by force or along a line, or a division
core_image: 一把斧头落在木头正中，年轮从裂缝向两侧展开
scene: 木场的圆木架上横着一段粗木。 The woodcutter split the log with a single clean stroke.
sceneCN: 这里 split 是「劈开」（第 1 个义项：沿一线用力分成两半）；句意为伐木工一斧利落劈开圆木。图中可辨识物件：圆木、斧头、木架。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「劈裂者；分裂者」
由动词现在分词作形容词，义为「剧烈的（头痛）；裂开的」
同义借词，义为「分叉」（书面）
近义借词，义为「（组织）分裂」

senses.title: To divide by force along a line
senses.definition: to break or divide something into parts, especially along a grain or seam
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成数块，尤指沿纹理或接缝
senses.example: The axe split the log down the middle.
senses.exampleCN: 斧头把圆木从中间劈开。
senses.why: One stroke follows the hidden line the wood already holds.
senses.whyCN: 一斧顺着木头里早已藏着的线落下。

senses.title: To divide into groups or parts
senses.definition: to divide into smaller groups or parts, especially by disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 分成更小的群体或部分，尤指因分歧
senses.example: The party split into two camps over the tax plan.
senses.exampleCN: 该党因税制方案分裂为两大阵营。
senses.why: The wood image lifts off the table: people, like grain, part along a line of strain.
senses.whyCN: 木材意象离开桌面：人群像木纹一样沿受力线分开。

senses.title: To share and divide up
senses.definition: to divide something such as money or work between people
senses.definitionCN: 在人们之间分摊钱物或工作
senses.example: We agreed to split the cost of the taxi.
senses.exampleCN: 我们说好平摊出租车费。
senses.why: Once something is divided, each piece belongs to someone.
senses.whyCN: 一经分开，每一份都有了归属。

senses.title: To end a relationship
senses.definition: to end a friendship, partnership, or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 结束友谊、合伙或婚姻
senses.example: The two founders split last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 两位创始人去年春天散伙了。
senses.why: The seam that held two things together finally gives way.
senses.whyCN: 维系两者的接缝最终崩开。

senses.title: A crack or tear
senses.definition: a crack or lengthwise tear in something
senses.definitionCN: 物体上的裂缝或纵向破口
senses.example: There is a long split in the old door panel.
senses.exampleCN: 旧门板上有一道长长的裂缝。
senses.why: The verb hardens into a noun: the line left by the blow is named.
senses.whyCN: 动词凝为名词：一击留下的线被命名。

senses.title: A division of opinion
senses.definition: a division or disagreement between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体间的分歧
senses.example: The vote revealed a deep split in the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 投票暴露了委员会内部的深刻分歧。
senses.why: The hidden grain of a group shows itself as a crack of opinion.
senses.whyCN: 群体隐秘的纹理以意见的裂缝显形。

senses.title: A share or portion
senses.definition: a part of a profit or sum that someone receives
senses.definitionCN: 利润或款项中某人所得的一份
senses.example: She took her split of the prize money.
senses.exampleCN: 她拿走了属于自己的一份奖金。
senses.why: Each half of the wood carries away its own weight.
senses.whyCN: 劈开的一半带走属于它自己的分量。

senses.title: Split second: a tiny moment
senses.definition: a very brief moment of time, as in a split second
senses.definitionCN: 极短的片刻，如一刹那
senses.example: The goalkeeper reacted in a split second.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员在一刹那间作出反应。
senses.why: Time itself can be divided, one hairline crack wide.
senses.whyCN: 时间本身也能被劈开，裂口只有发丝宽。

intro.en: Split is a native English verb of the axe and the seam, with relatives across the Germanic sea.
intro.cn: split 是斧头与接缝世界的本土英语动词，在海对岸的日耳曼语里有亲族。

items.en: *splīdan- is generally reconstructed as "to split, cleave"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *splīdan- 表示「劈开、裂开」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Dutch splitten and related Low German forms kept the same splitting image.
items.cn: 荷兰语 splitten 与相关低地德语形式保留了同样的劈裂意象。

items.en: The verb entered standard English in the sixteenth century from northern and maritime use.
items.cn: 该动词于十六世纪经北部及海上用法进入标准英语。

items.en: Some sources link it to Middle English splenten "to split wood", of the same Low German family.
items.cn: 一些辞源将其与中古英语 splenten「劈木」相联，同属低地德语词族。

items.en: The word now serves wood, groups, bills, hair and even time.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词服务于木头、群体、账单、头发乃至时间。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of dividing.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词；近义组收表示分开的动词。

entries.definition: One who or something that splits, or a device for dividing signals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指劈裂者或信号分配器。

entries.definition: British past of spill; one letter apart and a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: spill 的英式过去式；仅一字母之差，属另一个动词。

entries.definition: A narrow cut; shares the cutting image but has its own word history.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「切缝」；同属切割意象但词史独立。

entries.definition: A small quarrel or the past of spit; letters shuffled and of different line.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「小争吵」或 spit 的过去式；字母换位，词系不同。

entries.definition: Liquid scattering; begins like split but has another root.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「泼溅」；起首与 split 相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: The general word for separating into parts, without force implied.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体分开的通用词，不暗含强力。

entries.definition: A literary verb to split along a natural line.
entries.definitionCN: 书面动词，指沿自然纹路劈开。

entries.definition: To break with a sharp sound, often partly.
entries.definitionCN: 带着脆响裂开，常未断尽。

entries.definition: To cut off completely, especially a connection.
A sudden breaking apart, formal or medical.
entries.definitionCN: 骤然破裂，正式或医学用语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the axe image and the split forms the word really takes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用斧头意象，以及该词真实呈现的 split 形式。

normal.en: The verb never changes its clothes: split, split, split for past and participle.
normal.cn: 这个动词从不换装：过去式与过去分词都是 split。

normal.en: Split the bill is what friends say when sharing the cost.
normal.cn: 朋友分摊花销时说的是 split the bill。

normal.en: Split up can mean two people ending their relationship.
normal.cn: split up 可指两人结束关系。

normal.en: A split second is time cut as thin as a wood chip.
normal.cn: split second 是被劈得薄如木屑的一瞬。

normal.en: Splitting headache feels like the head itself has been cleaved.
normal.cn: splitting headache 感觉像头被劈开。

abstract.en: Picture the axe resting exactly on the line the grain drew long ago.
abstract.cn: 想象斧头恰好落在木纹早已画好的那道线上。

abstract.en: When a group splits, invisible grain becomes a visible crack.
abstract.cn: 群体分裂时，看不见的纹理变成看得见的裂缝。

abstract.en: Every split leaves two halves, and each half remembers being whole.
abstract.cn: 每次劈开都留下两半，而每一半都记得曾经的完整。

examples.en: They split the logs and stacked them by the shed.
examples.cn: 他们劈好木柴，堆在小屋旁。

examples.en: The committee split evenly on the proposal, six votes each way.
examples.cn: 委员会对该提案的表决正好五五开。

examples.en: Let us split the difference and each pay twenty.
examples.cn: 我们各让一步，每人付二十。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯普利特」——一斧顺着木纹落下：劈开；分裂

root: split 属日耳曼语源，一般认为原始日耳曼语 *splīdan- 表示「劈开」，与荷兰语 splitten 同族；经中古英语与北部、海上用法于十六世纪进入标准英语，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of split follow one axe stroke from wood to people to time: cleaving, dividing, sharing, and parting.
sensesIntro.cn: split 的义项随一斧落下，从木头走到人群再走到时间：劈裂、分化、分摊与分离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an axe falling along the line the wood has always held.
core.cn: 核心意象：一斧顺着木头一直藏着的那道线落下。

branches.en: THE WOOD LINE: force follows the hidden seam and things come apart.
branches.cn: 木材线：强力顺着暗缝，物体分开。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE LINE: groups crack along their own grain into camps and opinions.
branches.cn: 人群线：群体沿自身纹理裂为阵营与分歧。

branches.en: THE FAIR LINE: once divided, every piece has an owner.
branches.cn: 公平线：一经分开，每份各有其主。

branches.en: THE CLOCK LINE: even a moment can be split hairline-thin.
branches.cn: 时钟线：连一瞬也能被劈成发丝宽。

branches.en: THE BREAKING-AWAY LINE: seams give way and partnerships end.
branches.cn: 决裂线：接缝崩开，伙伴散伙。

intro.en: Split is a bare Germanic root; English adds only its own small endings around it.
intro.cn: split 是裸的日耳曼词根；英语只在它周围加自家的小词尾。

latinIntro.en: Split is Germanic in origin, so its Latin cognates list is empty; the Germanic root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: split 属日耳曼语源，因此拉丁同源词列表为空；日耳曼词根为重构形式。

items.example: The Dutch verb is a close relative.
It gives splitting with doubled t.
items.exampleCN: 双写 t 构成 splitting。
这个复合词把时间也劈开。

items.example: The dessert is named for its divided fruit.
items.exampleCN: 该甜品以剖开的香蕉命名。

items.example: The hair cracks like wood grain.

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「劈裂者；分裂者」
由动词现在分词作形容词，义为「剧烈的（头痛）；裂开的」
同义借词，义为「分叉」（书面）
近义借词，义为「（组织）分裂」

definition_zh: 靠垫；坐垫；缓冲物；缓冲，减轻
definition_en: a soft bag of cloth filled with padding, or something that softens a shock
core_image: 一个鼓鼓的软垫被塞在背后，整个人陷进去
scene: 她把一个软垫塞在背后，靠着墙坐下。 She put a cushion behind her back.
sceneCN: 这里 cushion 指「靠垫」（第 1 个义项：填充柔软、用来坐靠的垫子）；句意是她把靠垫垫在背后。

senses.title: A soft pad
senses.definition: a cloth bag filled with soft material, used to sit or lean on
senses.definitionCN: 装满柔软材料、用来坐或靠的布袋
senses.example: She put a cushion behind her back.
senses.exampleCN: 她把靠垫垫在背后。
senses.why: The body needs something between it and the hard frame.
senses.whyCN: 身体和硬框架之间，总得垫点东西。

senses.title: A buffer
senses.definition: something that absorbs a shock or protects against loss
senses.definitionCN: 吸收冲击或防止损失的东西
senses.example: Savings act as a cushion against hard times.
senses.exampleCN: 存款能在艰难时期起缓冲作用。
senses.why: A layer between you and the blow takes part of the blow.
senses.whyCN: 挡在你和打击之间的一层，会替你先挨一下。

senses.title: To soften a blow
senses.definition: to make a fall, shock, or loss less severe
senses.definitionCN: 使跌落、冲击或损失变得不那么严重
senses.example: The grass cushioned his fall.
senses.exampleCN: 草地缓冲了他摔下来的力道。
senses.why: Soft ground gives way, and giving way is what saves a body.
senses.whyCN: 软的地面会让开，而让开正是救人的地方。

intro.en: Cushion comes from Latin culcita, a mattress, through Old French coissin.
intro.cn: cushion 源自拉丁语 culcita（床垫），经古法语 coissin 进入英语。

items.en: Culcita named a stuffed mattress or sack.
items.cn: culcita 指填满东西的床垫或袋垫。

items.en: It also described a pillow for the head.
items.cn: 它也能指头下的枕头。

items.en: Coissin named a soft pad for sitting.
items.cn: coissin 指用来坐的软垫。

items.en: Cushion entered English for the pad of a seat.
items.cn: cushion 进入英语，指座位上的垫子。

items.en: The word grew a verb sense: to soften an impact.
items.cn: 这个词又长出动词义：缓冲冲击。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cush- opening, and the meaning group names other soft things that take a blow.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cush- 开头，近义组列出其他柔软、能替人挨一下的东西。

entries.definition: easy and comfortable, of a job
soft like a cushion
material that absorbs shocks
a soft support for the head
a thick soft piece used for protection
something that reduces a shock

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a soft square under a tired body and end with ground that gives way.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从疲惫身体下的一个软方块开始，落到一片会让开的地面。

normal.en: A cushion is a small promise that the seat will not hurt.
normal.cn: 靠垫是一个小小的承诺：这张椅子不会硌人。

normal.en: Put a layer between you and the blow and the blow arrives smaller.
normal.cn: 在你和打击之间垫一层，打击到了就变小了。

normal.en: Savings are a cushion made of money instead of cloth.
normal.cn: 存款是用钱而不是用布做的靠垫。

normal.en: Grass cushioned the fall because it let the body sink.
normal.cn: 草地能缓冲，是因为它让身体陷进去。

normal.en: Anything that softens a shock is doing a cushion's job.
normal.cn: 凡是让冲击变软的，都在干靠垫的活。

abstract.en: Picture a deep soft square on a wooden bench.
abstract.cn: 想象木长椅上放着一个厚软的方垫。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing into a cushion and leaving a shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按进软垫，留下一个凹痕。

abstract.en: Picture a jumper landing on a mat instead of concrete.
abstract.cn: 想象跳下来的人落在垫子上，而不是水泥地上。

examples.en: She put a cushion behind her back.
examples.cn: 她把靠垫垫在背后。

examples.en: Savings act as a cushion against hard times.
examples.cn: 存款能在艰难时期起缓冲作用。

examples.en: The grass cushioned his fall.
examples.cn: 草地缓冲了他摔下来的力道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cushion 记成「垫」：软的东西垫在身下，也垫在人和打击之间。

root: 源自拉丁语 culcita（床垫、垫袋），经古法语 coissin 进入英语；本义是填满柔软材料的坐垫，后来引申为一切起缓冲作用的东西与动作。

sensesIntro.en: From a pad under the body, to a layer against loss, to the act of taking the edge off a fall.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身下的软垫，到抵御损失的一层，再到把跌落的力道削掉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick soft square placed between a body and a hard surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块厚软的方垫，垫在身体和硬面之间。

branches.en: The first job is to make a hard seat bearable.
branches.cn: 它最开始的本事，是让硬座位能坐。

branches.en: Any layer that stands between you and loss becomes a cushion.
branches.cn: 任何挡在你和损失之间的一层，都成了缓冲物。

branches.en: The verb describes what the pad does to the blow.
branches.cn: 动词说的是垫子对打击做了什么。

branches.en: Cloth and savings do the same work at different scales.
branches.cn: 布垫和存款，在同一件事上做着不同尺度的工作。

branches.en: To cushion is to be the thing that absorbs the shock.
branches.cn: 缓冲，就是去做那个吸收冲击的东西。

intro.en: Cushion comes from a Latin mattress and has grown a small family of soft, easing words.
intro.cn: cushion 出自拉丁语的床垫，长出一小族表示柔软与缓和的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin culcita, a mattress, is the root behind cushion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 culcita（床垫）是 cushion 背后的根。

items.example: The cushion is old and flat.
The sofa came with two cushions.
The chair has a cushioned seat.

items.meaning: material or effect that softens shocks
items.exampleCN: 这双鞋需要更好的缓冲。

items.example: The moss was thick and cushiony.

items.exampleCN: 他找到一份轻松的差事。

items.example: The parcel was packed with an air cushion.

items.meaning: to make a shock easier to bear
items.example: The news was bad, but he cushioned the blow.
items.exampleCN: 消息很糟，但他把冲击缓和了一些。

definition_zh: 保留；保持；记住
definition_en: to keep something or continue to have it
core_image: 一只手紧紧握住一件东西，不肯松开
scene: 这家老店保留了许多传统做法，连包装纸都没有换过。 The old shop retains many traditional methods, and even its wrapping paper has never changed.
sceneCN: 这里 retain 是「保留」（第 1 个义项：继续拥有、不放弃）；句意：这家老店保留了许多传统做法，连包装纸都没有换过。

senses.title: Keep possession
senses.definition: to keep something and not give it away or lose it
senses.definitionCN: 保留某物，不送走也不丢失
senses.example: The museum retains the right to refuse entry.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆保留拒绝入场的权利。
senses.why: The Latin source means to hold back, so retaining is keeping a hold on something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为握住，因此 retain 就是继续握住某物。

senses.title: Continue to have a quality
senses.definition: to continue to have a quality or condition
senses.definitionCN: 继续具有某种性质或状态
senses.example: Thick walls retain heat in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 厚墙在冬天能保持热量。
senses.why: A quality that stays with an object is held in place, as if by a hand.
senses.whyCN: 留在物体上的性质就像被一只手按在原地。

senses.title: Remember information
senses.definition: to keep facts in your memory
senses.definitionCN: 把事实保存在记忆中
senses.example: Students retain more when they review often.
senses.exampleCN: 经常复习的学生记得更牢。
senses.why: Memory holds information the way a hand holds an object.
senses.whyCN: 记忆保存信息，就像手握住物品一样。

intro.en: Retain comes from Latin retinere, to hold back, from tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: retain 源自拉丁语 retinere（握住），由 tenere（握）构成。

items.en: Tenere means to hold.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住。

items.en: Retinere means to hold back or keep.
items.cn: retinere 意为拉住或保留。

items.en: Retenir keeps the sense of keeping.
items.cn: retenir 保留了「保留」的含义。

items.en: Retain means keep in possession.
items.cn: retain 意为继续拥有。

items.en: It also covers heat, memory and employees.
items.cn: 它也用于热量、记忆与员工。

note.en: Retain is close to keep and preserve, and shares a root with contain.
note.cn: retain 与保持、保存相近，并与 contain 同根。

entries.definition: the act of keeping
able to remember well
to keep someone waiting
to continue to have something
to keep something in good condition
to keep something at the same level

normalIntro.en: Retain is re- plus tain, hold: keep holding on.
normalIntro.cn: retain 是 re- 加 tain（握）：一直握着不放。

normal.en: Retain control means do not let go of power.
normal.cn: retain control 意为不放松权力。

normal.en: Retain information means keep it in memory.
normal.cn: retain information 意为把信息留在记忆里。

normal.en: Thick walls retain heat well.
normal.cn: 厚墙能很好地保温。

normal.en: Companies try to retain good staff.
normal.cn: 公司努力留住优秀员工。

normal.en: Compare maintain: maintain keeps a level, retain keeps possession.
normal.cn: 对比 maintain：maintain 保持水平，retain 保持拥有。

abstract.en: Picture a fist closed around a smooth stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手紧紧攥住一块光滑的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine warmth staying inside a wool coat.
abstract.cn: 想象温暖留在羊毛大衣里。

abstract.en: Think of a name written firmly in memory.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被牢牢写进记忆。

examples.en: The company retained its best engineers.
examples.cn: 公司留住了最优秀的工程师。

examples.en: Dark surfaces retain more heat than light ones.
examples.cn: 深色表面比浅色表面能保留更多热量。

examples.en: Few people retain every detail of a lecture.
examples.cn: 很少有人能记住讲座的每个细节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（一直）＋ tain（握住）」——一直握住不放，就是保留与保持；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回、持续）＋ tenere（握）→ retinere（握住不放）→ 法语 retenir → retain，核心义「继续握住、不失去」。

sensesIntro.en: Retain first means keep possession, then keep a quality, and finally keep information in memory.
sensesIntro.cn: retain 先指保留拥有，再指保持性质，最后指把信息留在记忆中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closed tight around something it will not release.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手紧紧攥住不肯松开的东西。

branches.en: Possession is the basic sense of keeping.
branches.cn: 拥有是「保留」的基本义。

branches.en: A quality stays in place like heat in a wall.
branches.cn: 性质留在原处，如同墙中的热量。

branches.en: Memory holds facts the way a hand holds objects.
branches.cn: 记忆保存事实，如同手握物品。

branches.en: Keeping an object often keeps its value too.
branches.cn: 保留物品往往也保住了它的价值。

branches.en: A retentive mind keeps what it learns.
branches.cn: 记性好的头脑能留住所学。

intro.en: Retain joins re- with Latin tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: retain 由 re- 与拉丁语 tenere（握）组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere, to hold, also gives contain, maintain and detain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere（握）也构成 contain、maintain 与 detain。

items.exampleCN: tenere 是表示握住的动词。
法语 retenir 传递了该词。
retentive 描述很强的记忆力。

definition_zh: 事情；事务；事件；私情；（口语）东西
definition_en: a matter that has to be dealt with, an event, a secret romantic relationship, or, informally, an object
core_image: 桌上一叠待办的文件，每一份都写着「这件事要处理」
scene: 客厅里两个人压低声音，茶几上的信件被推到一边。 The whole affair was settled before the guests arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 affair 指正在发生的这件事（第 1 个义项：需要处理的事情）；句意为客人们到来之前，整件事就已经处理妥当了。

pos.zh: 名词：事情；事务；事件；私情；东西

derivatives.zh: 由 love 与 affair 复合而成，义为「恋情；风流韵事」
由 current 与 affairs 复合而成，义为「时事；时政」
法语借形，与本词同源，指「事情、事件」，多见于仿法语书面表达

senses.title: A matter to be dealt with
senses.definition: an event or situation that has to be dealt with, often one that is complicated or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 需要处理的事情或局面，常指复杂或令人不快者
senses.example: The whole affair was settled before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们到来之前，整件事就已经处理妥当了。
senses.why: Old French afaire is literally 'to do', so an affair is whatever there is to be done, pictured as a task lying on the table.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 afaire 字面就是「去做」，所以 affair 就是眼前有待去做的任何事情，像桌上摆着的一份任务。

senses.title: Matters of business or public life
senses.definition: in the plural, the matters that belong to a person's business, a country's government or public life
senses.definitionCN: 用复数时，指属于个人业务、国家政务或公共生活的事务
senses.example: He handles foreign affairs for the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 他在该部负责外交事务。
senses.why: The same things to be done multiply: once they belong to an office or a state, the plural affairs becomes the standard word for its business.
senses.whyCN: 「要做的事」一旦成批出现，就带上了归属：属于某个机构或国家的那些事，复数 affairs 便成了固定说法。

senses.title: An event, often a scandal
senses.definition: an event or series of events that attracts public attention, especially one involving scandal or disgrace
senses.definitionCN: 引起公众关注的事件或一连串事件，尤指涉及丑闻或不光彩行为者
senses.example: The minister resigned after the affair became public.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事曝光后，部长辞职了。
senses.why: A matter that everyone talks about stops being private business and becomes a public event, and the word carries that weight without naming it.
senses.whyCN: 一件人人都在议论的事，就不再是私事，而成了公共事件；这个词不必点明，就自带那层不光彩的分量。

senses.title: A secret romantic relationship
senses.definition: a romantic or sexual relationship between two people, especially a secret one and often one that is disapproved of
senses.definitionCN: 两人之间的恋情或性关系，尤指秘密的、往往不被认可的那种
senses.example: Their affair lasted two years and ended badly.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的私情持续了两年，最后收场很难看。
senses.why: This is the matter kept off the table: something going on between two people that is deliberately not made public.
senses.whyCN: 这是被从桌面上收起来的那件「事」：两个人之间正在发生、却刻意不让外人知道的关系。

senses.title: An object, in informal use
senses.definition: an object or device, used informally and often with an adjective of approval or disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指物品或装置，常与表示褒贬的形容词连用
senses.example: He rode up on a smart little affair with a red tank.
senses.exampleCN: 他骑着一辆红色油箱的小玩意儿过来了。
senses.why: The vague 'matter' can shrink to a thing you cannot or will not name precisely, which is exactly the tone of this informal sense.
senses.whyCN: 含糊的「事情」可以缩小成一件你说不清或不愿细说的东西，这正是这个口语义的语气。

intro.en: Affair is a French noun made from a Latin phrase meaning 'to do', and its modern senses all descend from the idea of something that has to be done.
intro.cn: affair 是由一个意为「去做」的拉丁短语构成的法语名词，它今天的各个义项都源自「有待去做的事」这个观念。

items.en: *dhe- is generally reconstructed as 'to put, to do', and the Latin verb facere is usually traced to it; the deeper history remains source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *dhe- 意为「放置、做」，拉丁语动词 facere 通常被追溯到它；更早的历史来源不确定。

items.en: The recorded verb facere meant 'to do, to make' and built a very large family, including factum 'a deed' and efficere 'to bring about'.
items.cn: 有文献记录的动词 facere 意为「做、制造」，衍生出庞大的词族，包括 factum「行为、事迹」与 efficere「促成」。

items.en: The phrase à faire 'to do' became the noun afaire, meaning 'business, matter, thing to be done'. Latin had no such noun, so the formation belongs to French.
items.cn: 短语 à faire「去做」变成了名词 afaire，意为「事务、事情、有待去做的事」。拉丁语没有这个名词，因此这一构词属于法语阶段。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century as afaire or affaire; spellings varied for a long time, and the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，写作 afaire 或 affaire；拼写在很长时期内并不统一，确切的首次出现年代不确定。

items.en: The plural affairs became the standard term for business and public matters, while the singular kept the senses of event, secret romance and, informally, object.
items.cn: 复数 affairs 成为表示业务与公共事务的固定说法；单数则保留「事件」「秘密恋情」，以及口语中的「东西」等义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the plural, a French-style doublet and two words that only begin with the same letters; the near-meaning group holds words for a matter, an event, business and a secret relationship.
note.cn: 形近组收复数形式、一个法语借形，以及两个只是开头字母相同的词；近义组收表示事情、事件、业务与秘密关系的词。

entries.definition: The plural of affair, used as a fixed term for business, public matters or personal concerns.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的复数形式，固定表示业务、公共事务或个人事务，与单数「一件事」的分工不同。

entries.definition: A French-style spelling of affair used in English in phrases such as affaire d'honneur.
entries.definitionCN: 法语借形，与本词同源，见于 affaire d'honneur 这类仿法语说法，多用于书面语。

entries.definition: Friendly and easy to talk to; it merely looks similar and comes from a different Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「和蔼可亲的」；只是拼写开头相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 affabilis（ad 加 fari「说话」）。

entries.definition: A written statement sworn to be true; it only shares the opening letters and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宣誓书」；只是开头字母相同，词源不同，来自中世纪拉丁语 affidare（ad 加 fidere「信任」）。

entries.definition: A subject or situation that is being dealt with; the closest general word to affair.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事情、问题」，是与 affair 最接近的一般用词，但不含「私情」与「东西」两义。

entries.definition: Something that happens, especially something important; it has no sense of a task to be done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件、活动」，尤指重要的事，但不带「有待处理」的含义。

entries.definition: Matters that concern a person, a company or an organization; it overlaps with the plural affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事务、业务」，与复数 affairs 有重叠，但更偏商业与职责。

entries.definition: A single event, often unpleasant or unusual; narrower than affair and without the scandalous suggestion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件、事故」，多指单一而不快或异常的事，范围比 affair 窄，也不必然含丑闻意味。

entries.definition: A secret sexual relationship, or a working connection between groups; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「私通」或「联络」，前者与 affair 的私情义接近，但语气更正式、更隐晦。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French phrase behind the word and the fixed expressions it forms in modern English.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据这个词背后的真实法语短语，以及它在现代英语里构成的固定表达。

normal.en: afaire is à faire, 'to do': an affair is something on the to-do list.
normal.cn: afaire 就是 à faire「去做」：affair 是待办清单上的一件事。

normal.en: In the plural, affairs means the business of an office or a state.
normal.cn: 用复数时，affairs 指一个机构或一个国家的事务。

normal.en: A love affair is the matter kept off the table.
normal.cn: love affair 就是被收起来、不摆到桌面上的那件事。

normal.en: A scandal is an affair that reached the front page.
normal.cn: 丑闻就是一路闹到报纸头版的 affair。

normal.en: A smart little affair is informal for an object you do not bother to name.
normal.cn: a smart little affair 是口语说法，指一件你懒得细说的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of papers on a desk, each one stamped with the words to be done.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上一叠纸，每一张都盖着「待办」的戳。

abstract.en: One sheet can be lifted out and hidden in a drawer: that is the secret affair.
abstract.cn: 其中一张可以被抽出来锁进抽屉：那就是秘密的私情。

abstract.en: The same pile can belong to one person, to a ministry, or to a whole nation, and the word does not change.
abstract.cn: 同一叠纸可以属于一个人、一个部，或整个国家，而这个词本身并不改变。

examples.en: The dinner was a quiet affair with only close friends.
examples.cn: 那顿晚饭只请了亲近的朋友，办得很安静。

examples.en: She handles public affairs for the city council.
examples.cn: 她为市议会处理公共事务。

examples.en: Their secret affair was discovered by a colleague.
examples.cn: 他们的私情被一位同事发现了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费尔」——阿费尔把一叠待办纸拍在桌上：这些事都得处理。

root: 古法语 afaire「事情、事务」字面是 à faire「去做」，其成分可追溯到拉丁语 ad「朝向」+ facere「做」；英语复数 affairs 固定表示事务、业务。

sensesIntro.en: The five senses all start from something to be done: one task, a mass of business, an event people talk about, a relationship kept off the table, and the vague object nobody bothers to name.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都从「有待去做的事」出发：一件待办的事、成批的事务、被人议论的事件、藏在桌面下的私情，以及口语里那件懒得命名的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pile of papers on a desk, each one marked as something to be done.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一叠纸，每一张都标着「待办」。

branches.en: THE TASK: one thing on the table, waiting to be handled.
branches.cn: 任务线：桌面上的一件事，等着被处理。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: the tasks multiply and belong to a business or a state.
branches.cn: 机构线：事情成批出现，归属于一个机构或一个国家。

branches.en: THE HEADLINE: what everyone discusses turns into a public event.
branches.cn: 头条线：人人议论的事，变成了公共事件。

branches.en: THE DRAWER: one sheet is hidden away, and that is the secret relationship.
branches.cn: 抽屉线：其中一张纸被藏起来，这就是那段秘密关系。

branches.en: THE VAGUE THING: the matter shrinks to an object the speaker will not name.
branches.cn: 含糊线：事情缩小成说话人不愿点明的一件东西。

intro.en: Affair is built from Latin and Old French elements meaning 'to do'; English later added only a plural ending and a few compounds.
intro.cn: affair 由意为「做」的拉丁语与古法语成分构成；英语后来只加了复数词尾和少数复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, factum and the preposition ad are recorded; the Old French phrase à faire and the noun afaire are also recorded, and only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere、factum 与介词 ad 均有记录，古法语短语 à faire 与名词 afaire 也有记录，只有印欧词根属于重构形式。

definition_zh: 形成；组成；编队；地层
definition_en: the process of forming something, a group arranged for a purpose, or a layer of rock
core_image: 一行人排成整齐的队形，在操场上行进
scene: 云的形成需要水汽和冷空气。 The formation of clouds needs vapor and cold air.
sceneCN: 这里 formation 是「形成」（第 1 个义项）；句意：云的形成需要水汽和冷空气。

senses.title: The process of forming
senses.definition: the process by which something is formed
senses.definitionCN: 某物形成的过程
senses.example: The formation of clouds needs vapor and cold air.
senses.exampleCN: 云的形成需要水汽和冷空气。
senses.why: This is the central process sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的过程义项。

senses.title: An arranged group
senses.definition: a group of people or aircraft arranged in a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 按一定队形排列的人群或飞机
senses.example: The planes flew in formation.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机编队飞行。
senses.why: People and machines can be given a shape.
senses.whyCN: 人和机器都可以被赋予队形。

senses.title: A rock layer
senses.definition: a layer of rock with a particular structure
senses.definitionCN: 具有特定结构的岩层
senses.example: The cliff shows a rock formation.
senses.exampleCN: 悬崖上可见一处岩层。
senses.why: Geology names what time has shaped.
senses.whyCN: 地质学为时间塑造之物命名。

senses.title: A created body
senses.definition: a group or organization that has been formed
senses.definitionCN: 已经组建起来的团体或组织
senses.example: The formation of the club took a year.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部的组建花了一年。
senses.why: The process sense becomes a result.
senses.whyCN: 过程义项转化为结果。

definition_zh: 在楼上；到楼上；楼上的
definition_en: on or to a higher floor of a building
core_image: 楼梯尽头透出亮光，人一级级往上走
scene: 老房子一层招待客人，卧室全都放在木楼梯上面那层。 The children sleep upstairs and come down for breakfast.
sceneCN: 这里 upstairs 是「在楼上」（第 1 个义项：位于较高的一层）；句意为孩子们睡在楼上，早上下来吃早饭。楼梯尽头透光、人一级级往上走，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 把 up 换成 down 构成的反义形式，义为「在楼下」
复合词的后一部分的单数形式，义为「一级台阶」
复合词的前一部分，义为「向上」

senses.title: On a higher floor
senses.definition: situated on the floor above the one being spoken from
senses.definitionCN: 位于说话者所在层的上一层
senses.example: My grandparents live upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 我祖父母住在楼上。
senses.why: The word is simply up joined to stairs, so it names the place reached by going up a stair.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 up 与 stairs 的合体，指的是顺着楼梯往上到达的那一层。

senses.title: Towards a higher floor
senses.definition: used with verbs of movement towards the floor above
senses.definitionCN: 与运动动词连用，表示朝上一层去
senses.example: She carried the tray upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她把托盘端到了楼上。
senses.why: Where something rests, movement towards it also goes, so the same word marks both place and direction.
senses.whyCN: 某处既是所在之地，也是移动所向，因此同一个词既可标位置也可标方向。

senses.title: Used before a noun for a room above
senses.definition: used as an adjective before a noun naming a higher room
senses.definitionCN: 作定语放在名词前，指位置较高的房间
senses.example: The upstairs rooms get the morning sun.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上的房间有早上的阳光。
senses.why: Placed before a noun the same word works as an adjective, still pointing to the floor above.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前，同一个词就起形容词的作用，指向的仍是上面那一层。

senses.title: The upper floor as a place
senses.definition: used as a noun for the floor or part above
senses.definitionCN: 作名词指上面那一层或那一部分
senses.example: The upstairs needs painting this year.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上今年得刷一遍漆。
senses.why: A floor can be spoken of as a thing in itself, and the word then stands alone as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 一层楼也可以被当作一个独立的东西来说，于是这个词就单独作名词。

senses.title: A figure of speech for the mind
senses.definition: used informally of thoughts rather than places
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指「脑子里」而不是实际位置
senses.example: Whatever is going on upstairs, he shows nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 不管他脑子里在想什么，脸上一点也看不出来。
senses.why: Since the head is the top of the body, the floor above is borrowed for what goes on inside it.
senses.whyCN: 头是身体的最上面，因此「上面那层」就被借来说里面发生的事。

intro.cn: 一个朴素的复合词，由古老的「向上」副词与表示楼梯的名词合成。

items.en: Staer meant a stair, and up was the old adverb of upward motion.
items.cn: staer 意为「台阶」，up 是表示向上的古副词。

items.en: The plural staires named the whole flight rather than a single step.

items.en: Upstairs works as adverb, adjective, and noun without changing form.

items.cn: downstairs 以同一模式配上反义副词造出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普斯台尔斯」——阿普踩着每级台阶往上走，一路踩到楼上。

root: 英语复合词：up（向上）+ stairs（楼梯），stairs 源自古英语 staer（台阶）及其复数 staires（整段楼梯）

sensesIntro.en: One higher floor is reached, occupied, named, and finally borrowed for the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一层楼既可抵达、可居住、可指称，最后还被借去形容脑子里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light at the top of a stair.
core.cn: 核心意象：楼梯顶端透出的光。

branches.en: The place branch: where someone lives in the house.
branches.cn: 位置分支：人在屋里的落脚处。

branches.en: The direction branch: carrying something up.
branches.cn: 方向分支：把东西端上去。

branches.en: The attributive branch: a room on that floor.
branches.cn: 定语分支：那一层的房间。

branches.en: The noun branch: the part above the ground floor.
branches.cn: 名词分支：一层以上的部分。

branches.en: The figurative branch: what one thinks in secret.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：私下盘算的东西。

intro.en: Two transparent native pieces, with the second one older than it looks.
intro.cn: 两个透明的本土部件，其中后一个比看上去更古老。

latinIntro.en: Latin marks the upper part with the prefix super-, as in superiore parte.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用前缀 super- 表示上面的部分，如 superiore parte。

items.meaning: a set of stairs in a building

definition_zh: 仅仅的；只不过的；纯粹的；十足的；未掺杂的（古义）
definition_en: used to stress that something is no more than what is stated; also, in an older sense, pure and unmixed
core_image: 一杯没有兑水的酒，除此之外什么都没有
scene: 朋友兴冲冲地说起一个计划，其实那只是他昨晚随口想到的一句话。 His plan was a mere guess, not a real study.
sceneCN: 这里是「仅仅的、只不过的」（第 1 个义项：强调某物不过如此）；句意为他那个计划只是一个猜测，并不是真正的研究。图中可辨识物件：写满字的草稿纸、咖啡杯。

pos.zh: 仅仅的；只不过的；纯粹的；十足的

derivatives.zh: 由 mere 加 -ly 构成，义为「仅仅；只不过」，常用于修饰动词或整句
由 mere 加 -ness 构成，义为「仅仅是某种东西的状态」，较少使用

senses.title: Nothing more than what is named
senses.definition: used before a noun to stress that the thing is small, simple, or unimportant, and no more than that
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，强调该事物很小、很简单或不重要，不过如此而已
senses.example: The damage was a mere scratch.
senses.exampleCN: 损坏只不过是一道划痕。
senses.why: The Latin source meant pure, with nothing mixed in; from 'nothing added' it was a short step to 'nothing more than', which is how the modern word is used.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词源义为「纯粹的、没有掺入别的」，从「没有添加」到「不过如此」，只差一小步，现代用法正是后者。

senses.title: Sheer and absolute
senses.definition: used to emphasize that a quality is complete and nothing else is involved
senses.definitionCN: 强调某种性质完完全全，别无其他成分
senses.example: We met by mere chance at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站相遇纯属偶然。
senses.why: If mere means unmixed, then mere chance is chance with nothing else behind it, and the word naturally strengthens the noun it modifies.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mere 有「未掺杂」之义，mere chance 就是背后别无其他的偶然，这个词自然会给它所修饰的名词加上分量。

senses.title: Pure and unmixed (archaic)
senses.definition: in older use, describing a substance that has nothing added to it
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的用法中，形容某物质没有掺入任何别的东西
senses.example: The old recipe called for mere wine, with no water added.
senses.exampleCN: 那份旧食谱要求用纯酒，不兑水。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense: a liquid that is itself alone, and the modern 'only' sense is the same idea moved from wine to ideas.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的物质义：一种只由自己构成的液体；现代的「只不过」义，就是把同一想法从酒搬到了观念上。

intro.en: Mere as 'only' and mere as 'lake' are two different words that happen to share a spelling; the adjective came from Latin by way of French.
intro.cn: 表示「只不过」的 mere 和表示「湖」的 mere 是两个碰巧同形的词；形容词这一支经法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: Merus meant pure and unmixed, and it was used of wine that had no water in it.
items.cn: merus 意为纯粹的、未掺杂的，常用来形容不兑水的酒。

items.en: The neuter noun merum named unmixed wine itself, a small but vivid trace of the original sense.
items.cn: 中性名词 merum 直接指未兑水的酒，是原义留下的一个小而生动的痕迹。

items.en: Old French mier or mer meant pure and simple, and English borrowed it in the sense of unmixed.
items.cn: 古法语 mier 或 mer 意为纯粹、单纯，英语借入时取「未掺杂」之义。

items.en: Middle English used mere for pure and unmixed things, then weakened it to mean nothing more than.
items.cn: 中古英语用 mere 形容纯粹、未掺杂之物，随后弱化为「不过如此」的意思。

items.en: The lake sense comes from Old English mere, a different word altogether, and it survives mainly in place names.
items.cn: 表示「湖」的义项来自古英语 mere，完全是另一个词，如今主要保留在地名里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely resemble the spelling; the near-meaning group collects words that also mean 'nothing more than'.
note.cn: 形近组收只是拼写相像的词；近义组收同样表示「不过如此」的词。

entries.definition: To combine into one; from Latin mergere, to dip, so only the spelling resembles mere.
entries.definitionCN: 合并为一体；来自拉丁语 mergere（浸入），只是拼写与 mere 相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: A quality that deserves praise; from Latin meritum, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 值得称赞的品质；来自拉丁语 meritum，词源不同，仅拼写相近。

entries.definition: Soft wet ground; from Old Norse, a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 松软的湿地；来自古诺尔斯语，词源不同。

entries.definition: Happy and lively; from Old English myrige, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 快乐活泼的；来自古英语 myrige，词源不同。

entries.definition: And no one or nothing else besides.
Merely, with nothing more than that.
Complete and nothing else; used to stress a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 十足的、纯粹的；用来强调某种性质。

entries.definition: Complete and absolute, used of bad or surprising things.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的、绝对的，多用于糟糕或令人吃惊的事物。

normalIntro.en: The adjective began as a word for purity and ended as a word for 'nothing more'; a second, unrelated mere still means a lake.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词从「纯粹」出发，最后表示「不过如此」；另有一个毫无关系的 mere，仍然指「湖」。

normal.en: Merus in Latin means unmixed, so mere wine was wine with no water added.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 merus 意为未掺杂的，所以 mere wine 就是不兑水的酒。

normal.en: The step from 'unmixed' to 'nothing more than' is easy: if nothing is added, then there is nothing else.
normal.cn: 从「未掺杂」走到「不过如此」并不难：既然没有添加，也就没有别的了。

normal.en: Merely is mere plus -ly, and it is the adverb you want when you mean 'only', not the adjective before a noun.
normal.cn: merely 是 mere 加 -ly，当你想说「仅仅」而修饰动词时用它，而不是用放在名词前的形容词。

normal.en: The lake mere comes from Old English and survives in names such as Windermere.
normal.cn: 表示「湖」的 mere 来自古英语，保留在 Windermere 这类地名里。

normal.en: Mere words is a common phrase because words alone, with no action, are exactly what mere means.
normal.cn: mere words 是常见搭配，因为只有话、没有行动，正是 mere 所表达的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of wine with nothing poured into it, then move that 'nothing added' idea onto a guess or a scratch.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯什么都没兑进去的酒，再把「没有添加」这个想法挪到一个猜测或一道划痕上。

abstract.en: Mere always shrinks the noun after it: the word itself is a small spotlight aimed at something small.
abstract.cn: mere 总是把它后面的名词缩小：这个词本身就是一盏照向小东西的小聚光灯。

abstract.en: One spelling for 'pure' and 'lake' shows how English lets two unrelated lives share a single coat.
abstract.cn: 「纯粹」与「湖」共用一个拼写，说明英语能让两个毫不相干的身世穿同一件外衣。

examples.en: The damage was a mere scratch.
examples.cn: 损坏只不过是一道划痕。

examples.en: We met by mere chance at the station.
examples.cn: 我们在车站相遇纯属偶然。

examples.en: The old recipe called for mere wine, with no water added.
examples.cn: 那份旧食谱要求用纯酒，不兑水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米儿」——只剩一粒米儿，少得可怜；mere 就是仅仅的。

root: 拉丁语 merus（纯粹的、未掺杂的，尤指不兑水的酒）经古法语 mier 进入英语；另有一个来自古英语 mere 的同形词，意为「湖」，二者无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is 'nothing added'; it yields the everyday 'nothing more than', the emphatic 'sheer', and the archaic literal 'unmixed'.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「没有添加」；由此得到日常的「不过如此」、加强语气的「十足」，以及古老的字面义「未掺杂」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass of wine with nothing poured into it, pure and alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯没有兑入任何东西的酒，纯粹而孤立。

branches.en: a scratch too small to matter
branches.cn: 一道小得不必在意的划痕

branches.en: two people meeting by chance at a station
branches.cn: 两个人在车站偶然相遇

branches.en: a glass of wine with no water in it
branches.cn: 一杯没有兑水的酒

branches.en: the same 'nothing else' said of size and of cause
branches.cn: 同一种「别无其他」，一处说大小，一处说原因

branches.en: an old recipe that insists on the pure liquid
branches.cn: 一份坚持要用纯液的旧食谱

intro.en: The adjective rests on a Latin word for purity, its noun for unmixed wine, and an English adverb suffix that turns it into merely.
intro.cn: 这个形容词依托一个表示纯粹的拉丁词、一个指未兑水之酒的名词，以及一个把它变成 merely 的英语副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: A Latin adjective of purity and its noun for unmixed wine lead through French to the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 表示纯粹的拉丁形容词及其指未兑水之酒的名词，经法语通向英语形容词。

definition_zh: 复杂的；综合体；情结
definition_en: made of many connected parts that are hard to understand, or a group of buildings, or a strong feeling fixed in the mind
core_image: 一团缠在一起的线，越拉越紧
scene: 新小区里有住宅、商铺和一所小学，走进去容易迷路。 The new complex includes homes, shops and a school.
sceneCN: 这里 complex 指「综合体」（第 2 个义项：由多部分组成的建筑群）；句意是这个新综合体包含住宅、商铺和一所小学。

senses.title: Hard to understand
senses.definition: having many parts that are connected in ways hard to follow
senses.definitionCN: 由许多部分以难以理清的方式相连
senses.example: The tax rules are far too complex for most people.
senses.exampleCN: 税法对大多数人来说太复杂了。
senses.why: Many parts plus many links is exactly what makes a thing hard to hold in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 部分多、牵连多，正是事物难以在脑中把握的原因。

senses.title: A group of buildings
senses.definition: a group of buildings or facilities used for one purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为同一用途建起的一组建筑或设施
senses.example: The sports complex has two pools and a gym.
senses.exampleCN: 这个体育中心有两个泳池和一间健身房。
senses.why: Parts gathered on one site become a whole that carries one name.
senses.whyCN: 聚集在同一场地上的部分，成了一个共用一个名字的整体。

senses.title: A fixed feeling
senses.definition: a strong feeling or idea that is fixed in a person's mind
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢盘踞在人心里的强烈感受或念头
senses.example: He still has a complex about his accent.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己的口音仍有心结。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word for feelings woven so tightly that they hold the mind.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借这个词，指缠绕得紧紧、抓住人心的感受。

intro.en: Complex comes from Latin complecti, to embrace or intertwine, whose participle is complexus.
intro.cn: complex 来自拉丁语 complecti，意为拥抱或交织，其分词形式是 complexus。

items.en: Plectere meant to weave or to twine.
items.cn: plectere 意为编织或缠绕。

items.en: Complecti meant to wrap around and hold together.
items.cn: complecti 意为缠绕包围、抱在一起。

items.en: Complexus described things woven into one.
items.cn: complexus 描述被织成一体的东西。

items.en: English complex first meant made of connected parts.
items.cn: 英语 complex 最初指由相互连接的部分组成。

items.en: It expanded to building groups and to fixed feelings.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到建筑群以及盘踞不去的感受。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close to complex in sound, and the meaning group ranks complicated, intricate and a network of parts.
note.cn: 形近组收的是读音与 complex 相近的词，近义组排出复杂难懂、错综复杂与相互连接的部分。

entries.definition: the natural colour of the skin
to finish something
to confuse someone
hard to understand because of many parts
having many small parts arranged finely
a group of connected things

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with tangled thread, then move to many buildings on one site and to a knot held in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从缠住的线开始，再走到同一场地上的一片建筑以及心里的一个结。

normal.en: Com- is together and plex means weave, so complex is woven together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，plex 是编织，complex 就是被织在一起。

normal.en: Many parts plus many links equals complex.
normal.cn: 部分多、连接多，就等于复杂。

normal.en: A sports complex is one site holding many facilities.
normal.cn: 体育综合体就是一块场地上装着许多设施。

normal.en: An inferiority complex is a knot that keeps pulling tight.
normal.cn: 自卑情结就是一个越拉越紧的结。

normal.en: Complex is the thing; complexity is the quality it has.
normal.cn: complex 是那个东西，complexity 是它具备的性质。

abstract.en: Picture a ball of thread where one pull tightens everything.
abstract.cn: 想象一团线，一拉反而更紧。

abstract.en: Picture one gate opening onto homes, shops and a school.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门后连着住宅、商铺和学校。

abstract.en: Picture a single thought that keeps returning at night.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头，夜里总是回来。

examples.en: The human brain is a highly complex organ.
examples.cn: 人脑是一个极其复杂的器官。

examples.en: They built a new shopping complex near the station.
examples.cn: 他们在车站附近建了一个新的购物中心。

examples.en: He has a complex about being short.
examples.cn: 他对个子矮有心结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 complex 记成 com（一起）加 plex（编织）：许多线一起编在一块，就是复杂的。

root: 源自拉丁语 complecti（缠绕、拥抱）与 complexus，本义是交织在一起的，后引申为复杂的、综合体与情结。

sensesIntro.en: From many tangled parts, to many buildings on one site, and finally to a knot in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 从交织的许多部分，到同一场地上的一片建筑，最后到心里的一个结。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball of thread tangled so tightly that pulling makes it worse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团缠在一起的线，越拉越紧。

branches.en: Many parts and many links make the first sense.
branches.cn: 部分多、连接多，造出了第一个义项。

branches.en: Buildings gathered on one site carry the same name.
branches.cn: 聚在同一场地的建筑沿用同一个名字。

branches.en: A feeling woven that tightly becomes a complex.
branches.cn: 一种感受缠得那么紧，就成了情结。

branches.en: Both senses gather parts into one whole.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把部分聚成一个整体。

branches.en: A tangle in the world and a tangle in the mind share one image.
branches.cn: 世上的乱麻与心里的乱麻共用一个意象。

intro.en: Complex is built on Latin com, together, plus plectere, to weave.
intro.cn: complex 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 plectere（编织）构成。

latinIntro.en: The weaving base also appears in perplex, to weave someone into confusion.
latinIntro.cn: 表示编织的词基也出现在 perplex 里，意为把人织进困惑。

items.meaning: more than one complex or complex feeling
items.example: The city has three sports complexes.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市有三个体育中心。

items.example: The complexity of the rules surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 规则的复杂程度让我们吃惊。

items.example: She explained the complexities of the case.
items.exampleCN: 她解释了案子的复杂之处。

items.meaning: the natural colour of the skin
items.example: The sea air improved his complexion.
items.exampleCN: 海边的空气改善了他的肤色。

items.example: People of all complexions work here.
items.exampleCN: 各种肤色的人都在这里工作。

items.meaning: a problem that makes things harder

definition_zh: 腰带；地带；传送带
definition_en: a strip worn around the waist, or a long narrow area
core_image: 工人系紧皮带走进车间
scene: 他系紧皮带，把工具包挂上去。 He tightened his belt before climbing.
sceneCN: 这里 belt 是「腰带」（第 1 个义项：系在腰上的带状物）；句意是他爬之前系紧了腰带。

pos.zh: 动词：用带子系住；（口语）猛击

derivatives.zh: 由 belt 加 -ed 构成，义为「系腰带的」
由 belt 加 -ing 构成，义为「传动带材料」
由 belt 与 way 复合，义为「环城公路」

senses.title: A strip around the waist
senses.definition: a strip of leather or cloth worn around the waist
senses.definitionCN: 系在腰上的皮革或布带
senses.example: He tightened his belt before climbing.
senses.exampleCN: 他爬之前系紧了腰带。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, borrowed from Latin for a strap.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，借自拉丁语中表示带子的词。

senses.title: A long narrow area
senses.definition: a long region with a special feature
senses.definitionCN: 具有某种特征的长条区域
senses.example: This city sits in the industrial belt.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市位于工业地带。
senses.why: A belt wraps around, so a wide band of land took the name.
senses.whyCN: 腰带是环绕的，因此一大片带状土地也得此名。

senses.title: A moving strip in a machine
senses.definition: a continuous strip that carries things
senses.definitionCN: 连续运转、用来运送物品的带子
senses.example: The boxes moved along the belt.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子沿着传送带移动。
senses.why: The shape of a waist belt matches the loop inside machines.
senses.whyCN: 腰带的形状与机器里的环形带一致。

intro.en: Belt came into Old English from Latin balteus, a strap.
intro.cn: belt 经拉丁语 balteus（带子）进入古英语。

items.en: balteus meant a girdle or strap.
items.cn: balteus 意为「腰带、带子」。

items.en: belt named a waist strap.
items.cn: belt 指腰间的带子。

items.en: belts held tools and swords.
items.cn: 腰带用来挂工具和剑。

items.en: machines gained moving belts.
items.cn: 机器开始使用运转的带子。

items.en: belt also names long regions of land.
items.cn: 如今 belt 也指狭长的地带。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group gives strap and zone words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是带子与区域的词。

normalIntro.en: A belt is a strip that holds things together or marks a band of land.
normalIntro.cn: belt 是能把东西束住的带子，也能指一条带状土地。

normal.en: The plural is belts.
normal.cn: 复数是 belts。

normal.en: A seat belt keeps you safe in a car.
normal.cn: seat belt 让你在车里更安全。

normal.en: Tighten the belt also means spend less.
normal.cn: tighten the belt 也指节省开支。

normal.en: An industrial belt is a factory region.
normal.cn: industrial belt 指工业地带。

normal.en: The verb means to fasten with a belt.
normal.cn: 动词义指用带子系住。

abstract.en: See a worker pulling a leather belt tight.
abstract.cn: 想象工人把皮带勒紧。

abstract.en: See factories lined along a wide road.
abstract.cn: 想象沿大路排开的工厂。

abstract.en: See boxes rolling on a moving strip.

examples.cn: 他爬之前系紧了腰带。

examples.en: This city sits in the industrial belt.
examples.cn: 这座城市位于工业地带。

examples.en: The boxes moved along the belt.
examples.cn: 箱子沿着传送带移动。

dict_mnemonic.text: belt 读起来短而紧，正像一条勒紧的腰带。

sensesIntro.en: The same strip wraps a waist, a machine and a stretch of land.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一条「带」束住腰、绕住机器，也圈出一片土地。

definition_zh: 强调；着重；使突出；重读
definition_en: to give special importance to something; to make a word or feature stand out
core_image: 用手指重重敲在桌上的那一行字上
scene: 发布会上，负责人把安全两个字重复了三遍。 The report emphasizes the need for care.
sceneCN: 这里 emphasize 是「强调」（第 01 个义项：给予某事特别重视）；句意是报告强调需要谨慎。

pos.zh: 及物动词：强调；着重；使突出

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ize 得到名词，义为「强调；重点」
由同一词干加 -atic 构成，义为「强调的」
由 emphatic 加 -ally 构成，义为「强调地」

senses.title: To give special importance
senses.definition: to state or show that something is especially important
senses.definitionCN: 说明或表明某事特别重要
senses.example: The report emphasizes the need for care.
senses.exampleCN: 报告强调需要谨慎。
senses.why: The verb is emphasis turned into action, so to emphasize is to make one point show forth from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是 emphasis 变成动作，所以 emphasize 就是让某一个要点从其余部分中显现出来。

senses.title: To stress a word in speech
senses.definition: to say a word or syllable with extra force
senses.definitionCN: 用额外的力度说出某个词或音节
senses.example: She emphasized the word never.
senses.exampleCN: 她重读了「绝不」这个词。
senses.why: Voice can do what a spotlight does, so the verb also names the act of striking one syllable harder.
senses.whyCN: 嗓音也能做聚光灯做的事，所以这个动词也指把某个音节读得更重。

senses.title: To make something visually prominent
senses.definition: to make a feature more noticeable in a design or image
senses.definitionCN: 让设计或图像中的某个特征更引人注意
senses.example: The designer emphasized the logo with a bright border.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师用亮色边框突出了标志。
senses.why: If importance can be shown by voice, it can also be shown by color and line, so the verb reaches visual design.
senses.whyCN: 如果重要性可以用声音表现，也就能用颜色与线条表现，于是这个动词延伸到视觉设计。

intro.en: Emphasize is a nineteenth-century English verb built on the Greek-derived noun emphasis.
intro.cn: emphasize 是十九世纪英语在希腊来源的名词 emphasis 基础上构成的动词。

items.en: The noun meant a showing forth.
items.cn: 这个名词意为显现、显露。

items.en: Latin borrowed the noun from Greek.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入该名词。

items.en: English emphasis arrived in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 emphasis 在十六世纪进入。

items.en: English added -ize to make the verb emphasize.
items.cn: 英语加 -ize 构成动词 emphasize。

items.en: The verb now covers speech, writing and visual design.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个动词涵盖口语、写作与视觉设计。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emphasis family; the near-meaning group separates stress, highlight and underline.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emphasis 词族展开；近义组区分加重、突出与划线。

entries.definition: Special importance or vocal stress.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「强调、重点」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: Forceful and certain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「强调的、断然的」。

entries.definition: In a forceful way.
To give force to a word or point.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强调、重读」，与 emphasize 很接近。

entries.definition: To draw attention to something as the most important part.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「突出」，强调把某部分挑出来。

entries.definition: To mark a line under text, or to stress a point.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「在下面划线」，也比喻强调。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read emphasize as making something show, then let the showing work through speech, text and design.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 emphasize 读成「让某物显出来」，再让这种显现通过说话、文字与设计起作用。

normal.en: Emphasize is the verb behind emphasis.
normal.cn: emphasize 就是 emphasis 背后的动词。

normal.en: The -ize ending means to make or put into action.
normal.cn: -ize 词尾表示「使……、付诸行动」。

normal.en: You can emphasize a point with repetition.
normal.cn: 你可以用重复来强调一个要点。

normal.en: You can emphasize a word with your voice.
normal.cn: 你可以用嗓音重读一个词。

normal.en: You can emphasize a logo with a bright border.
normal.cn: 你可以用亮色边框突出一个标志。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tapping the same line three times.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在同一行字上敲了三下。

abstract.en: The verb turns attention into an action.
abstract.cn: 这个动词把「注意」变成一个动作。

abstract.en: Emphasize is emphasis set in motion.
abstract.cn: emphasize 就是被启动的 emphasis。

examples.en: The report emphasizes the need for care.
examples.cn: 报告强调需要谨慎。

examples.en: She emphasized the word never.
examples.cn: 她重读了「绝不」这个词。

examples.en: The designer emphasized the logo with a bright border.
examples.cn: 设计师用亮色边框突出了标志。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安法塞子」——像塞子一样把重点堵在眼前

root: 由 emphasis 加动词词尾 -ize 构成；emphasis 经拉丁语来自希腊语，由 en-（在内）加 phainein（显示）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Emphasize makes a point important, a syllable loud and a feature visible.
sensesIntro.cn: emphasize 让一个要点变重要、一个音节变响、一个特征变醒目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tapping one line to make it stand out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指反复敲同一行字，让它凸显。

branches.en: THE POINT: importance stated in words.
branches.cn: 要点线：用话语说明重要性。

branches.en: THE VOICE: one syllable struck harder.
branches.cn: 声音线：把某个音节读得更重。

branches.en: THE DESIGN: a border or color draws the eye.
branches.cn: 设计线：边框或颜色吸引目光。

branches.en: WRITING AND SPEAKING: the same push on paper and in air.
branches.cn: 写与说：同样的推力落在纸面与空气中。

branches.en: WORD AND IMAGE: both can carry the spotlight.
branches.cn: 文字与图像：两者都能承载这束光。

intro.en: Emphasize is emphasis plus -ize, the verb ending meaning to make or act.
intro.cn: emphasize 是 emphasis 加 -ize，这个词尾表示「使……、去做」。

latinIntro.en: The root goes back through Latin to Greek phainein, to show.
latinIntro.cn: 词根经拉丁语追溯到希腊语 phainein（显示）。
